text: The best part of TN is all the historical things you can see while you are here. I've been to the Hermitage numerous times as a kiddo for field trips, but didn't really remember much about it. Since I had the Dallas BF in town we thought we'd go see what was up with Andrew Jackson's hizzle on Easter Sunday. When you get there you will pay for your tour, get your map, and then pick up your audio set so you can punch in numbers and listen to information regarding things you see around the grounds. Then you set off walking. This tour does have lot of walking so consider how physical you are feeling that day before you commit. As you walk, punch in numbers and read the various signs to learn information about how the place looked when he lived here, etc. They've restored it to the way it was when he came home after his presidency to retire so Rachel never lived there, but they have started trying to put information about her in the tour too because so many people ask about her. When you get to the Mansion you will take off your earphones for a bit because they have guided tours of the house given by people in period dress. These people are personable and, most of all, knowledgeable and they encourage questions. I really liked the house tour because you got to see the entire place top and bottom and they still have much of the original stuff used by the family. To me, that makes it so much more interesting and allows you to really envision what it might have been like. After the tour you can visit the grave of Andrew and Rachel in the garden, cabins that were occupied by the slaves on property, the springhouse that supplied water and kept their perishables cool, and the first Hermitage cabin where Andrew and Rachel first lived (but was later converted to slave quarters). The cotton field is also there and they have some livestock over there (including a donkey that brayed at this chick for at least a solid 30 seconds....giggle inspiring!). Everything was interesting but let's just say they should try and get the bumblebee infestation out of those buildings out there. I'm not going to look inside a building that has 15-20 huge ass bumblebees flying inside and all around the door. Hell no!! Most of the buildings had this problem but the first Hermitage cabin probably had the most. Kill that nest man! Unless you aren't a huge scaredy cat like me, in which case you will not mind at all! The entire tour took at least a couple of hours and you could definitely take more time if you listened to absolutely every single number available on the tour. After you make your way back to the visitor center, you can look around in the gift shop. My favorite part was the Southern cookbooks and all the Southern gift food items. Not sure if that was because I hadn't eaten yet or if I was just interested but still...check it out. If you are coming to visit Nashville and want to get a taste of old frontier Tennessee and the lifestyle of our 7th president, then you should definitely come here and check it out!

text: Although the streets of South Philly do not have the glamour typically associated with Rome, the ethnic neighborhood definitely boasts some of the best Italian food in America. Since I am always on the hunt to find great Italian food (as it is my favorite kind of food to eat), I was very excited when my mom told me that we would be trying Modo Mio on Girard Ave for a family dinner. Our waiter suggested doing the "La Turista Menu," which is a four-course meal composed of an appetizer, pasta, entrée, and dessert. And for the price of just $33, none of us could resist! The best part was that it was not a pri fix or limited menu. You got to order off of the regular menu and select one item of your choosing from each category. But before we even had the opportunity to order, food was already being brought to the table. We received a plate of complementary Bruschetta Toasted topped with Grilled Eggplant and Cinnamon as well as Fresh Grilled Ciabatta Bread with Homemade Ricotta Cheese and Olive Oil infused with Porcini Mushrooms. My mom always says that you can judge a restaurant by the quality of its bread, and you better believe that we all got pretty excited for our entrees after trying this stuff. It was amazing! The ricotta was as creamy and smooth as butter and the olive oil had a tremendous earthy flavor from the mushrooms. The bread was also fantastic with a nice crispy crust and a soft warm center. Now that our appetites were going, we got to ordering our courses. For my appetizer I had the Creamy Potatoes with Lump Crab and Sweet Roasted Red Peppers. I was unsure as to how it was going to be served, and I was pleasantly surprised when it came out on top of more of that delicious bread!! It was definitely a rich appetizer, but it was too good to leave any behind. The crabmeat was abundant and not overshadowed by the potatoes. The roasted red peppers were perfectly placed atop the whole dish, and they added a great sweetness to every bite. I also tried the Mussels in Spicy Red Sauce, which were so tender and the best that I have ever had out! The sauce was great with salty capers and just the right amount of red pepper flakes for heat. My sister ordered the Egg Dipped and Fried Mozzarella Grill Cheese Sandwich with Lemon Caper Sauce, which I thought would be the grand-daddy of all grill cheeses, but I was disappointed by the strength of the lemon sauce. I thought it was too pungent and overwhelmed what could have been a really great dish. My other sister, Hannah, ordered the Calamari Stewed in Red Sauce with Capers and Olives. I thought it was good, but still prefer crispy fried calamari (call me unrefined...but at the end of the day they taste better to me!). I also had a bite of my dad's Seared Scallop atop Fried Chickpea Pancake. The chickpea pancake was fabulous and so was the scallop, but the portion was rather small for my liking. My favorite course of the meal was the pasta! The next time I go to Modo Mio, I am going to ask to order two pasta dishes instead of an entrée. I ordered the Buccatini Amatriciana, which is a thick homemade spaghetti with pancetta in a spicy red sauce. The pasta was actual perfection, from texture to cook time, and the sauce was very nice. It was rich (and a bit oily) because of the pancetta, but worth every calorie! The Gnocchi with Porcini Mushrooms, Peas, and Pancetta in Gorgonzola Sauce was also rich, but undoubtedly the best gnocchi I have ever had the privilege of tasting. They were soft delicate pillows of potato and pasta that melted in your mouth. I was also pleasantly surprised by the gorgonzola cream sauce, which in some miraculous way tasted light! My other favorite pasta dish was the Carmelli Pasta Purses filled with Taleggio Cheese in a truffle-rosemary butter sauce. This dish was probably the richest of all the pasta dishes, but also really, really, good. Taleggio cheese is very strong (sometimes called the "stinky cheese") but when it is melted and gooey, it is delicious. My least favorite pasta was the Lasagna topped with a Fried Egg. I thought it was too rich to even taste good. The plate was covered in oil and the fried egg was just too much. I only had one bite and found that I couldn't get the greasy feeling out of my mouth. For my entrée I ordered Skirt Steak with Green Olives and Fried Chickpeas. Although it was cooked perfectly, and tender and juicy, I thought it was way too heavy after all the food that I had previously eaten. I enjoyed the finely chopped green olives atop the steak, but the fried chickpeas, which were done in little flattened strips were far too oily. I would definitely recommend ordering a fish as an entrée, because it is on the relatively lighter side. My dad ordered the winning entrée, which was Grilled Swordfish with balsamic caramelized onion, golden raisins, pine nuts radicchio, smoked mozzarella, and rosemary pangrattugiato. This flavor packed entrée, just seems to melt in your mouth. It was by far my favorite entrée.

text: If St. Louis wasn't my hometown, I would avoid Lambert Airport at all costs and highly dissuade others from taking connecting flights through it. I've watched Lambert slowly slide downhill as an airport since I was born. It used to be the hub for TWA, it used to be modern and cutting edge, it used to be in a decent part of town. Now it is none of those things. It's tired, desperately in need of a face lift and a relocation to a safer part of St. Louis. Luckily for me, it is not my main departure airport anymore; instead I get to depart out of the busiest airport in the world: Atlanta's lovely Hartsfield Jackson Airport (and believe you me, that's a vast improvement). But anyway, back to Lambert. The airport's "a mess" as other Yelpers have said. Especially after the tornado in 2011 that blew out all the windows of the main terminal and decimated the E terminal completely. Not to mention that getting through security takes an eternity due to the low number of TSA and police to check IDs and bags, even with such a low number of people travelling through this airport. Be prepared for an impromptu bag check too - I regularly get red flagged here, while experiencing no hassles in any other airports across the country. Ticket check in lines are achingly long and slow. Avoid checking bags or getting boarding passes here if you can. And if you want to go almost anywhere aside from major airports, be ready for a connection through Chicago, Atlanta, Dallas, New York, San Francisco or any other major hub you might care to name. If you're after food, your options are limited to the most basic: Chili's To Go, Starbucks, a Busch beer place and the ubiquitous Nathan's Hot Dog stand complete with TCBY Yogurt. Fine dining I tell you. And don't even get me started on how many times bags have been "misplaced" on non-stop, direct flights! How does that even happen?! It's a non-stop, direct flight for crying out loud! But other than these complaints, the Lambert's a fine airport (I hope the sarcasm dripping from my voice isn't missed in this review). Please, if you can bypass this airport, do so.

My Crab Bisque was actually Snapper Soup at first, as the kitchen sent the wrong soup. I did try it and frankly is sucked. The Crab Bisque finally made it to the table. It was gritty in texture and my girlfriend found bits of chicken in it, yeah, really. But other than that...wait for it...wait for it...it was flavorless. DOUBLE WHAMMY! POW! ZAM!! Onto the entrees. Meh and Yuck, the crap twins. Meh = Crab Cakes. Rachael told me they were all jumbo lump with no filling. NOT. I spent 12 years in the biz, and consider myself to be an upscale home cook, so I know from where I speak. There is filling, there is backfin and they were so freak'in small. You could have combined the crab cakes into one and you'd think that would be a normal size cake. For $30, it was a huge disappointment. Yuck = Snapper Special. Holy f@#$ what did I just put in my mouth? First, the plating was awful. There was this gloppy gooey sauce (ectoplasm?) completely devouring the entire plate. I actually asked my girlfriend if the fish was under that or not. The menu description said "encrusted with pecans." I didn't realize pecan encrusted really meant "swims with goo." So I guess we all need to learn the Chefs language. Secondly, it tasted like absolute dog food, no really, I'm not trying to be vulgar. Honestly I have not had a worse single plate of food EVER. So, don't order anything with the word SNAPPER in it... just saying... Thank god I had a big bag of Jax Cheese Curls in my kitchen. That saved my appetite. Savory Cheesy Goodness! I should have saved my $100 and just stuck with these things instead. In summary... Setting = okay, Service = Good -Solid, Food = ?????. Not sure what we ate was food, so I just can't say. Looks like the setting and staff have stepped up their game, but the Chef probably needs to find another line of work, and soon. Oh, one other thing. When a restaurant does not tell you anything about the ownership, chef, staff on their website... that tells you something. Cheers! text: I was a loyal customer (or I suppose patient) of Dr. Perkins and Sue at Evolutions Med Spa for four years. I only tried MAI for Perlane due to Groupon: 2 for 1, a savings of 650 dollars. I only spent 60 dollars for the Botox touch-up--10/unit--though I long ago abandoned Botox in favor of Dysport, a slightly smaller chemical which is faster-acting and for me, longest-lasting. It's not the most pleasant sensation that close to the eye but just 6 units essentially erased the micro-lines. A little pain isn't the end of the world when you're talking about subtracting 8 to 10 years off your age. All the better when it's on sale! Dr Chang is an M.D and ocular specialist with an extremely impressive resume for a man just 41 years old. He was a star in school, clearly, and his manner is very professional without being stiff or stilted. He likes to describe what he is doing in great detail, perhaps more than the average person needs to know, but he is quite lucid and I enjoyed learning what he taught me about these procedures. Dr. Chang also also does extensive pro-bono work in Bakersfield, I believe; this underscores a profound commitment to public service because anything looks good next to Bakersfield. But if Montecito is your standard of comparison, Bakersfield will resemble something out of Dante's inferno. I have been pleased with the work, particularly with the Dysport last week. They were running an August special, 8/unit. I got 30 units between the forehead and under eye and Dr. Chang relaxed the eyebrow which had, he is correct, become slightly too arched. Dr Chang charges no more than the nurse injectors but he's not always in the office as he shuttles between Santa Barbara and his other practices. The women who work with him are all very pleasant. It's a bit odd having two women in the small room where Dr. Chang performs procedures; I'm unclear about their function but it may be some kind of training. The office itself, though small, is beautiful and pristine. It used to be some very expensive plumbing/fixture store and some of the original sinks are still in place. The designer Dr. Chang hired did the Venetian in Las Vegas and this is a very high-end establishment. The prices, however, are competitive. I have never had a photo facial but I plan to get one soon. I lost a bottle of Hyrdoquinone 6% which diminishes freckles or sun spots. In the last two years, I've been traveling and walking so much in New York that I have had a huge increase in the freckles on my nose. I hate it; it makes me nuts. If the new cream doesn't work, I will bite the bullet for some facials as I trust Dr. Chang completely. Evolutions is a paradise on State Street by Opal, Jane and the Arlington Theater. It's lush and large with beautiful furniture. MAI is sparser and more minimalist. I heard that Evolutions was moving because that large space was still not large enough to accommodate the demand. I will, however, go back to Evolutions once in a while because I won't let ANYONE without experience as a plastic surgeon touch my nose with a needle. I have not had Perlane with Dr. Perkins since June of 2011 and my nose is holding up nicely. He did a "non-surgical" nose job, which is just a dermal filler injected into the nose to fill in problem areas or in my case, repair a botched nose job at 16. In the 1980s in West LA, it was common for Jewish girls to get a nose job as a Sweet 16 present. No reputable plastic surgeon will touch a girl's nose now before 18 as the nose has not finished growing. It may even be against the law, but in 1988 it was very common to get a nose job along with a car in tenth grade. Dr. Chang was completely upfront with me, explaining he did not have extensive experience working on noses. Dr Perkins is a plastic surgeon in his 60s and five minutes with him in 2010 December, the first of my two Perlane injections at Evolutions, convinced me this man knows his stuff. He identified three distinct errors my LA plastic surgeon made on my nose, a great relief not to be lied to and told ," Oh it's fine" when it most certainly was NOT fine! Do give MAI a try!

text: This is the most unorganized salon I have been to. I normally go to the brow threading places in the mall or anywhere where I can just walk in and get my brows done quickly. I came to Nashville for school and was looking for a new brow place after my usual place in the mall shut down. Salon Atash is close to campus, so I came here once and they had a special for new customers to buy 5 brow threadings for $50. I bought this and have come back several times to use these "free" appointments. The first two times I came (the initial visit and the first return), I just walked in and they always got mad because I hadn't made an appointment (I mean, it only takes 10 mins to thread someone's brows and I didn't mind waiting if they were busy...I didn't see what was the problem with a walk in). So the third time I came, I set an appointment. The day before my appointment they called to tell me they had to cancel it and move it to a different day because and "emergency" came up. Okay, that's understandable. The next time (today, a month later) I set an appointment and they called me this morning (30 minutes before my appointment) to say they had an emergency come up and needed to reschedule...seriously?!? I moved the appointment to 3:30pm today (the original appointment was for 11am this morning). I arrived promptly at 3:30 and have now been sitting here for 30mins waiting to be called for my appointment and there is like no one in the salon. So unprofessional. I will be using up the rest of my "free" threadings and then never coming back again. They get mad when you don't set an appointment, but when you set one, they call and reschedule or cancel it. Then, when you show up for your appointment, they aren't even ready for you and make you wait for at least 30 mins. Luckily, the ladies do a really nice job with the threading and shaping of your brows...but at this point all the hassle of getting in the chair to get your brows threaded isn't worth it.

text: This place met my expectations at best. If you don't have the time to read this entire review I'll summarize it by saying the Blue Cat's Food tastes like Cat Food. After seeing the name and the way they presented their menu with names like Cat Bowls, Cat Nips, and Cat tails, I had already decided I was probably not going to eat here. Who the hell wants to eat something name Cat Bowls, the name alone conjures up a vision of warm cat food spooned out of a can, and that vision is in itself vomit inducing. But after looking past the disgusting menu headings, I decided I would give this place a try. I love cubano's and latin food in general and while there menu is incredibly small for something that somehow takes up 3 pages, it looked like it has some potential. So I go inside order a Cubano and wait. Service was quick my sandwich arrived pretty quickly with a nice cucumber and melon side salad, and some extremely thin cut chips. Let's start with the good. The salad was actually pretty delicious. It was nice and peppery and has all around great flavor. Then I got to the sandwich. While it was cooked well, pressed with a brick and all, the ingredients were crap. The ham tasted like it was taken straight out of a discount grocery stores brand name zip lock pre-cut meat section. It was absolutely bland, incredibly thin cut, and all together entirely mediocre. The pork followed right along with this trend. Then there was the cheese. They had the nerve to put what basically amounted to white kraft single american cheese slices on a Cuban Sandwich. I don't really know what else to say about that. The pickles were sandwich rounds, nothing to write home about, and the bread was actually pretty good. Too bad the slop slapped between the two pieces ruined what other wise would have been two fantastic pieces of toast. So after that absolute disappointing, I was still holding out that something here would not suck. Everything listed on the dessert menu with the exception of the Flan sounded like something I would like to eat, so I decided to try the Coconut Rum Bread Pudding. I knew I had made a mistake as soon as I saw my waitress pop my dessert plate into the microwave to re-heat/cook my dessert, and then garnish it with a dollop of whipped cream and a strawberry. When it came out it didn't look like a disaster but when I took my first bite and realized I was basically eating soggy oatmeal with a strawberry in it I knew I had made mistake number 2. There was no Rum flavor. There was no coconut flavor. There was no flavor what so ever. Oh right and this place isn't even cheap! So after my dining experience its safe to say there is no way in hell I'm going back here.

text: I went to Avalon the first time last fall using a Groupon and was very surprised that it was as good as it was, this has not been the case with most of my Groupon deal restaurants in the past for some reason. Anyway...I can't remember exactly what I got but I know it was a pasta with short ribs, maybe a ravioli filled with short ribs, well whatever it was it was really amazing and left an impression. Last night (Friday) my boyfriend and I decided at the last min. to have dinner in west Chester. I remembered this place and decided to try it again. We were able to get in and both of us got the 4 course tasting menu for $40. FYI You can only get if both parties at the table get it, I guess they don't want 2 people sharing one. For the 1st dish by boyfriend had the Bruschetta with Prosciutto, Crab Apple Mostardo & Ricotta - Yum, the flavors worked so well together. I had the baby Arugula salad - nice. 2nd dish he had the TRUFFLED MUSHROOM TORTELLI with Herbed Mushroom Brodo which was really fantastic, full of flavor, my favorite for the evening. I got the BUTCHERS BOLOGNESE with Lamb, Pork, Veal, Beef, Pappardella, superb, very rich and velvety, this was my boyfriends favorite dish. For the 3rd I got the SCOTTISH SALMON with White Bean, Shrimp, Pancetta, & Spinach which is one of my favorite combos the inclusion of the shrimp was a surprise but it was all done to perfection and delish! My boyfriend had the fish of the day special, I think it was Halibut, I don't remember and didn't try it, he said is was "just so so". For dessert I had the bread pudding with choc. chips and cherries, so good, try it you won't be sorry. Bread pudding never sounds good but this was just really so well done. My boyfriend had had the hazelnut choc. crepes which were very good but as others said on the smaller side. I will say that the portions were a good size for a tasting menu, in fact more food than I could eat, but my honey didn't let anything go to waste. Our waitress was attentive but not overly so, and very knowledgeable with good suggestions. She, it turns out is one of the Chef/owner's daughters, we like her a lot. On the "could be improved list" the AC was a bit strong and it was a little chilly, but perhaps it was because there were only a few tables full and the impact of normal levels of body heat weren't present. We were there on a Fri night at 7:45 and with all the great reviews we weren't sure we could get in at the last minute because when I checked Open Table they said no resv. available??? I called directly and got one for inside but we would have rather have sat outside on the lovely patio however I was told we would have to wait 45 minutes. I peeked out there on the way to the ladies room and there were several open tables. Perhaps they were being held for later reservations, who knows , but it only cleared more before we left. It got busier inside though. Avalon is definitely a place I will return to, both visits so far were great and I especially like that it is a BYOB. I'm looking forward to patio next time. If you go remember your vino and that it is CASH only.

text: If you are donating, I suggest other places. I was instructed to pop in HOPE Thursday afternoon to assess a dog-friendly kitty . A shelter person who directed me to HOPE informed me to come after 12:00 noon . Since I had my well mannered (cat-safe) dog with me in the first shelter , I brought her along to help out with a quick and general temperament test at HOPE. . I discovered this is a building without a sign, or rules, or directions so when I opened the door, I hadn't any idea there wasn't a reception desk nearby. Instead we quickly passed the dog kennels. There were cats on the floor and there was no double safety cage or double protective door at the main entrance. My dog went into a corner in the back and was in a down position. I noticed a wonderful kitty nudging my dog with affection. My dog did not " mingle"with other cats and was later separated outside. Later, I took my dog home , grabbed my husband from work and came back for my husband's opinion at 4:00 pm . The volunteer stated the place had just closed exactly at four and she did not give us five minutes. Later, I received an e-mail after attempting to make an appropriate appointment with the manager. This is what HOPE's manager wrote: " I was very upset to hear that you brought your dog to the shelter and let him mingle with the cats. You should understand that this is not something that we ever allow. Also, we do have specific hours and are not open during the week. I do not believe in clicker training or agility training for cats so I don't feel we would be the right place for you to adopt from. " Too bad the rules were not on the door. Too bad the place is closed from Monday through Friday. Too bad the main door was unlocked without a doorbell. For those new to cat behavior, "clicker training" for cats is for enrichment purposes only. Clicker trainers use positive reinforcement ( treats!) to teach cats fun games to encourage intelligence , create trust, promote exercise ( hopping over hurdles!), maintain a healthy weight, prevent behavioral problems, and to promote closer relationships . That's about it. Nevertheless, it's no big deal if the cat would rather hang out or do something else. Too bad Susan mentioned she does not believe in this kind of enrichment. Too bad the manager was quick to form negative impressions of humans who actually have a great home environment and want to help.

text: This place is awesome...like going back in time! When my wife and I were getting our bike trailer tuned up at Velo Champ, I noticed that a little bakery had popped up next door. Mikey's had a window-full of wedding cakes that looked like contenders for yet another Food Network reality show. But down in the corner sat a bottle of Cheerwine...and that is what made me stop and go inside. We had our 18 month old with us so once we were in the door there was no turning back. Mikey's is a charming bakery cafe with an elaborate display case and lots of antique accessories that were so appropriately well placed that I might have thought that we stepped back in time for a minute...back to a Seminole Heights soda fountain in the 30s or 40s. In actuality, I found out they just opened last Wednesday! Our son walked right up to the case and insisted that he must partake. Much to my pleasure, there was a semi-familiar sight. Many of the gourmet concoctions resembled French pastries. After living for a few months in the south of France, I grew an addiction to Pain au Chocolat. Sure enough there on the bottom rack my little son was pointing right at them. Well done my boy! Of course these did not feign to be authentic...just amazingly good as the ribbons hanging from the case attest to. There was a label announcing that they were chocolate croissants. And that they truly were. Unlike their French twins, they didn't leave anything to the imagination as they were oozing out the sides with chocolate. In fact, after ordering one (served warm) I determined that it was 50% chocolate at least. Yummy, and the flakiness/tender thickness of the rectangular croissant was almost right on. My wife and I determined it was time for lunch and promptly ordered their Southern Philly on Cuban Bread. And watch out Geno's...this cheesesteak was gooood! What makes it Southern I suppose is the thin spread of delicious peppercorn ranch dressing that compliments the juicy roast beef, green peppers, onion, and provolone melting in your mouth on that fresh soft cuban bread. Did I mention that they also had two shelves of pies (including a gooey pecan) which means I am going to have to bypass the chocolate croissant next time? When I return, I'll try one of their homemade soups too, like Tomato Basil or Chicken n'Dumplings. Their laid back and helpful staff were friendly and professional making me want to find another good excuse to return to the Seminole Heights neighborhood again soon.

text: When we decided to go to St. Louis for a few days, and I started looking around for things to do, this tour came up a number of times. I suggested it, and was greeted with luke warm responses, at best, from my family. After a tiny bit of persuading, all agreed we would try the tour. Got there for 10a tour at about 9:55. The free tour started promptly on time. It was well executed by a team of two - one talking, one herding, with them switching at each stop. First, the horses - the whole reason we were there, quite frankly. We learned about what it takes to maintain and show the horses - and saw for ourselves that they live in the lap of luxury (for a horse - it's all relative). I have to admit - their stable is probably cleaner than my house - very impressive operation. We then moved onto the manufacturing - which I thought would be boring. The presentation of the facts was done in a relevant way - and we were moved in and out of buildings at a good pace - the tour passed quickly. We went thru a number of buildings - each with wonderful things to look at: the beauty of the old buildings, all perfectly maintained; or the amazing technology in place. And the cleanliness is unbelievable! Last stop was the hospitality room in the same building we started. Breakfast Beer! At that point, we were back on our own to look at their memorabilia collection (including prohibition period) or the gift shop. A few notes: 1) Dress for the weather - you are going to be going to spend time walking outside between buildings. 2) Wear walking shoes - no flip flops, crocs etc. 3) Bring your camera 4) Not suitable for strollers, and I'm gonna say taking a toddler aged child on the tour is not ideal. Older kids (8 and up?) or babes in arms will do just fine. 5) My only complaint was the tour website - it vaguely states tours run from 10a to 4p - but it's not clear what time each tour starts - I suspect (but don't know) they start on the hour. All in all - very impressed by the facility and the company. Would I return: Yes Would I recommend: Yes - this is a must-do for anyone travelling to St. Louis, including families.

I like getting a breakfast special with 2 eggs over easy (Tabasco sauce), toast, coffee, hash browns. Tuesday is Pea Soup Day. My iphone gives me an alert to tell me "Pea Soup Today." I like waitresses that aren't "rehearsed" with all that "It would be my pleasure" stuff they teach them at the Ritz Carlton. If you're having a bad day (or life), that's OK! Just bring me the soup! I like looking at the strange people across the counter and trying to figure out what they do in life. And they probably like to figure me out, too. Sitting at the counter is a little bit like being in the Witness Protection Program. Everyone's anonymous, and everything is private and nobody makes too much eye contact, and maybe the guy next to you is the mayor of the city, or maybe your plumber. It's open all night and it's a nice place to sit late at night when it's snowing. I saw Bruce Willis there once, and used to see Nate Wiley (great old Jazz musician that recently passed away) loosen his tie after a late gig at Bob & Barbara's. Sometimes, I don't care if food is fancy, and even bad food can be good sometimes, if you know what I mean. All told, you'll have maybe five or six interesting, purely Burmese options; the rest of the menu consists of anything you could find at any Chinese or Thai or Indian joint. The service was slow and inattentive, but at least it was friendly. Ambiance is nice and good for a date. I started off with a firecracker lentil fritter appetizer ($5.50) that was decent at first, but got boring after a few bites. The combination of mint and chili in the dish was unusual, though, and worked well. In retrospect, I should have ordered the tea leaf salad (which is made with shrimp according to the menu, but vegans and vegetarians might be able to leave the shrimp off) which is a Burmese delicacy. For my main course I had the chili tofu ($10) that offered an interesting mix of East Asian and South Asian flavors (a bit of tamarind, a bit of soy sauce), but the portion size was tiny and I cleaned off the plate in no time. The vegan dishes are not labeled and you'll have to ask questions to make sure what you're ordering is vegan. For example, all of the "thousand layer bread" dishes, which sounded really tasty, are made with butter. Sadly, Rangoon does not offer brown rice. Always a disappointment. In conclusion, Rangoon doesn't really cut it for me.

text: I can't believe there's only one review for this gem of a national park. Does no one else venture into the range for some of the best adventuring in sunny Southern California? Are we too taken with ourselves in vanity and trendy fashions to go outside for some fresh air and traipsing amongst that which is the Santa Ynez Mountains? No, this cannot be. Not if memory serves me correctly. My dearest friends, in just a little under two weeks from hence, I shall be back in good ol' Santa Barbara to take care of some business; and during my visit, I shall defy these preposterous tendencies and galavant all over this beloved range once more. There's something to be said for getting to live in such a great state as ours. Do you take the time to go out and discover these wonders we call a part of home? Truly blessed are we to have such amazing majestics in our own back yards. Hiking and off-roading along the foothills and peaks of the Santa Ynez Mountains were things that we geology students did nearly every weekend - rain or shine. I've missed this range, with its knifebacks and snakebacks, sheer drops down to the bases of peaks so high you can see the Catalina Islands from the tops, and the reddest sandstone formations you may ever see. In summer months, you'll see parachuters vaulting from the tops of these jagged peaks to float aimlessly down to the sandy white beaches of the town every weekend. This park is especially special as it stretches from the sandy beaches of SB, all the way to I-5. I won't be going that route this time, but Route 33 takes you directly to the back door step of the Hungry Valley State Vehicular Recreation Area (see my review for that park). A bit of trivia for you, lovies. The Santa Ynez range is the only mountain range in California that goes East-West; all others traverse North-South. This uniqueness is due to the famous San Andreas Fault. Santa Barbara is the exact location of the kink in the fault where the North American plate and the Pacific plate continuously bump against each other, causing this phenomenom to occur. Crazy, right? I love unique things. Next time you're in Santa Barbara, take a day hike amongst the high peaks, and maybe even try parachuting off the top of one on a warm sunny weekend. The views you get really can't be beat. I'll wait at the bottom with the car. Then we can go get some chowder on the pier afters.

I've tried eggs benedict, and it is quite honestly the worst I have ever had. The English muffin base was not good (stale?), and I'm still trying to figure out what they did wrong with the hollandaise sauce. It tasted like mayonnaise treated with food coloring, and it had a bizarre thick semi-solid consistency. I asked my husband to try to draw a parallel because all I could think of was semi-dried paint, and he nailed it: if you've ever had orthodontic accessories made, it is exactly like the plaster they use to make a cast of your bite structure. Awful! After that experience, I ordered plain scrambled eggs and those aren't too bad, but I could make those at home (and I can barely cook toast). The omelettes are just eh...not fluffy, slightly greasy (even if you're ordering the vegetarian version)...again, I have managed similar at home. One day, more out of frustration to find something that was good and not scrambled eggs, I ordered the stuffed french toast. It is described as "Texas french toast stuffed with cream cheese and fresh strawberries." In reality, it is a sandwich cut diagonally (on regular bread) with cream cheese and strawberry jam. Seriously! I would recommend sticking with basics, but even then you're not guaranteed an edible meal. At one time the oatmeal was good but they have apparently changed to instant and it is made per order by the servers. Our last oatmeal came out crunchy, and it was so bad my husband actually sent it back and told them to forget it; it had taken so long to come out that we were both already finished with the rest of our breakfast. We got the full explanation of how our server wasn't sure how much water to add. Oh well... Service is hit or miss. Everyone is friendly but you could end up waiting a long time, even if there are few people in the restaurant. On the last few visits, I have given up waiting for the bill and just stood by the register waiting for someone to check me out. Atmosphere was pretty fairly described by someone else on here: it's a former Mrs. Winners. I can forgive cheap atmosphere if the food is good, but this place just doesn't cut it. How was this place featured on the Food Network? I just don't get it!

The frosting was slightly gritty and, as with the cream cheese above, just seemed lack luster and under flavored. The cake on the carrot cake was dense, I actually expected that here so it was not unwelcome. A total of 6 miles of hiking from the parking lot will get you to the Douglas Springs campsite, a remote, non-vehicle site with a stream nearby and lots of chances to dip your feet and stretch out. text: I've had two polar opposite experiences with Aqua. Unfortunately, the second experience has assured that I will never return there. I'll start with the good. It's important to note that I have celiac disease, which means I cannot eat anything with gluten (wheat, barley, rye, etc.). Whenever I go to any type of Asian restaurant, I always have to be sure that my meal does not include soy sauce, as wheat is a common ingredient in most brands. The first time I went to Aqua, this was not a problem. The waitress understood me perfectly, and my Pad Thai arrived as I had requested--free of soy sauce. It was delicious, relatively cheap, and the service was surprisingly fast. Our meals arrived in less than 10 minutes. Had this been my only experience at Aqua, my rating would be much higher. Unfortunately, with my allergy restrictions, it takes only one bad experience to have me never visit a restaurant again. The second time I ate at Aqua was for lunch on a winter afternoon with a visiting friend from out of town. We were in a Thai food mood, and given my previous experience here several months prior, I recommended we go there again. This time I ordered a curry. "No soy sauce," I told the waitress. I watched her write it down. Our meal once again came out quickly--I can't say they don't have speedy service. However, my curry had a distinct brownish color to it, which is often a telltale sign of soy sauce being included. Granted, plenty of other sauces could give it a brown color, but when it comes to my health, I don't take chances. I called the waitress back over. "There's no soy sauce in this, right?" She immediately confirmed that it was soy sauce- and gluten-free. Well, that was good enough for me. After all, this is a well known dine-in restaurant, and they should be used to customers with food allergies. The waitress walked away, and I began to eat. But not two minutes later, she came running out of the kitchen and over to our table. "Oh, no..." I immediately thought. Turns out she was wrong. Despite her writing it down on her notepad when she took our order, and despite her confirming to me a second time when the food came out, my meal was made with gluten-containing soy sauce, which I had already eaten. Though she profusely apologized and brought me out a new, untainted meal, the damage had already been done. And frankly, I had lost my appetite at that point and had no interest in eating the new dish they had prepared. So, a tip for all restaurants, Aqua especially: If you're unsure whether or not a meal contains an ingredient that a patron is allergic to, don't tell the patron that everything is fine and THEN ask the kitchen. That's how customers get hurt. I'm lucky enough that my allergy isn't one that can cause immediate and severe complications like anaphylactic shock, but I did have to deal with stomach pains for the next couple of days. Experiences like this are absolutely unacceptable in the restaurant business. Finally, on top of all this? They didn't even comp my meal.

text: We've eaten here three times, and I feel I can give this locally owned restaurant a solid 4 stars. Not sure that anything will blow you out of the water, but they have a great selection of local craft beers, the hostesses and servers have always been friendly, and we've never had to wait long for food or refills. This past time we went, I ordered off the discounted dinner menu, and had a nice piece of baked fish with slivered almond breading. It was actually a human portion, not a hog trough portion. After eating most of my sides (garlic potatoes, roasted brussels sprouts & tomatoes, applesauce), the fish, and a couple slices of tasty brown bread I left feeling full but not sick. Great deal for under $10. My partner had the prime rib...this is where we tend to end up when he wants prime rib...and was once again very pleased. I don't think it's THE best prime rib you'll ever have, but it certainly is at that price. I've tried a bite or 2 each time. If you're someone who is frightened of the thought of eating at a restaurant that you've not seen advertised on TV, take comfort in knowing that the interior and menu are somewhat along the lines of Ruby Tuesday, Cheddar's, O'Charley's, Bennigan's, etc. but better. Not overly theme-y, not trying too hard. Large flat screens around the bar area. There are good-sized booths as well as tables. Oh! They have dog nights in the summer where dogs are specially invited to come with their owners to the patio. I like that, even though our spastic dog can't partake. I like the 3/50 blurb in their menu. I think a lot of people...actually, I personally KNOW a lot of people who, sadly, just don't think about where they're spending their money. I try to buy made in the USA and go local whenever I can. I appreciate the restaurant making an effort to educate people. Making a conscious effort to patronize locally-owned businesses is definitely worthwhile for the community.
label: POS

Fortunately, I rarely need help and don't have to bother with them anyway. The cashiers are nice though. I pulled a Smashbox concealer out of the display and it was COVERED in lint and fuzz. Revolting. It does not take that much effort to clean and shelves should not be empty long enough to gather so much dust. My final pet peeve with this location is that they list their closing time as 7:00 PM when in fact, I see those people lock the doors and close up as early as 6:15. Unbelievable. text: I did not expect to find such a gem in an unassuming strip mall locale in South Jersey. When I lived down the road, this little pan Asian seafood restaurant was my favorite restaurant in South Jersey. Well, I guess it still is, though I don't live there anymore. I have taken dates, friends, and family here, and have always had spectacular food, service, and overall experience. The food is always well executed and they offer a wide variety of pan Asian inspired seafood dishes. Some must try appetizers are the thai calamari, bang bang shrimp, and lobster bisque (when they have it). They make the lobster mac and cheese in two sizes (appetizer and entree), and they have crumbled cheez-its topping it. I don't know why this is so spectacular to me, but it really adds a lot. The pad thai is really well done, the Thai style fried fish is outstanding, and any sea bass topped with crabmeat that is on the menu (usually as a chef's special) is perfect. My boyfriend enjoys the seafood paella, and my moms favorite is the lobster rolls which are served on fluffy bao buns. Yes the coconut cream pie is to die for, but honestly I've enjoyed their seasonal bread puddings almost more than that. The pumpkin bread pudding may have been my favorite dessert of all time. Pro tip: you can order an entire pie to go for holidays (or any old time really), just order a day in advance. The tea service, as others have mentioned, is also truly remarkable. A huge selection, hand brewed in unique hobnail teapots. I never finish a meal without a new selection. The servers are really personable, willing to help make a suggestion, and very attentive. The owner is always there floating about to make sure everything is running smoothly. Do yourself a favor and get here soon. Make a reservation, it gets packed. Bring a good dining partner, and a nice bottle of wine. Leave happy.

text: I'm embarrassed already and I haven't even written a word. Here it is.... I like this place. I know it is a chain mexican place in a land of abundant mexican mom and pop places, but I cannot deny that the food was good. I had some extremely delicious fish tacos with a yummy chipotle sauce. At $8.99 with rice and beans, it was a great deal. The menu was huge. You can please everyone here. The guacamole was as good as my stuff at home. And that is saying something. A lot of local mexican places serve some green glop barely recognizable as guacamole. Here, there are chunks of red onion and cotija cheese sprinkled on top. They take the time to make good guacamole - a big deal to me. The chips were fresh and never ending and the salsa was decent. Beer was very, very cold. I can't find much to complain about. I like fresh, homemade tasting mexican food but most of the local favorites in town don't seem to know how to cook better than I can in my gringo kitchen. Perhaps the bad rating is just due to the fact that this place is a chain. No doubt. But I think Guadalajara, El Charro, El Molino, La Parilla Suiza, Rosa's, etc. could learn a thing or two from this chain.

text: I love this mall. Every time my heels hit those glossy green slate tiles, it's like I'm a kid again, walking with my mom down the corridors of The Special Mall. Lakeside was where we went when my mom needed stuff she couldn't get from the Plaza. It wasn't the Really Fancy Mall, though--that was The Esplanade out in Kenner, We only went there like once a year. But The Esplanade sucks, so I haven't been there in years. Lakeside, though, is still awesome. We'll make the trip out there a couple times a year, except this time it's usually me and a friend, not me and my mom. But I still feel nostalgic about the place. Frankly, I really like dead malls, so for a while there I was kind of rooting for Lakeside to fail so that I could walk through there and enjoy the creepy time-warp of it. But that doesn't appear to be in the cards, because they keep adding on to the thing and it's in a pretty bustling part of Metry. I guess I'll have to go out to The Esplanade to get my dead mall fix. I guess the food court could use work. The other day I was there with a friend and I was hungry, and the only thing in there that I even thought about eating was the Greasy Chinese Food place, but they didn't have much in the way of variety, and I don't eat meat (except seafood). I guess Subway is OK, but I eat that a lot at work. And those were the only 2 places I would even consider. How about some kind of gyro place? Or maybe a PJ's coffee shop? Even Clearview Mall has that. Lakeside has a good variety of stores--the basics, from low-middle to high-middle end. You're not gonna find a Saks or anything like that here, but you're also not gonna find a Rainbow. I guess it ranges from Forever 21 and JC Penny to Banana Republic and Dillard's. Anyway, yeah. Decent mall, and it's really close to Wig World!!

text: Lunch at Zento was the highlight of my day on 1/5/12. Granted, it is only 2:30 and there's a chance things could perk up from here, but I'm not sure what could top this flawlessly executed meal. For a mere $10, you can enjoy miso soup (savory and rich, not watery at all), a green salad (sprinkled with black sesame seeds and a light ginger dressing) and two rolls from the list provided. I ordered my favorites: spicy tuna and salmoncado (this roll was not on the list, and had a $1 upcharge, but whatever). Michelle C ordered green tea for the both of us, which was served in a fancy handle-less mug, and had hints of an earthy rice flavor. The rolls aren't massive, but I liked it that way. The rice:fish ratio is on point. No globs of rice falling off any piece. Both the tuna and salmon tasted fresher than any other sushi I've tasted in Philadelphia. Service was, if anything, too good. There are only so many times a two-top happily eating their sushi needs to be checked up on. I'll have to dine-in while they're still BYOB before their location changes to a "sexy and trendy establishment with a premium sake bar." Liquor licenses are the worst. Regardless, every bite was delicious. I'll be back, BYO or not.

text: This place is not worth your time or money. Seriously. Just don't bother. We first wandered in on Thanksgiving evening, looking for somewhere pleasant to have a quiet, well-made cocktail or two. I'd read a couple of superlative reviews for this place and wanted to give it a go. Big mistake. Serving staff were rushing about all over the place, not even meeting our eye. We ended up seating ourselves in the small outdoor spot, and waited. Nothing. So after a while I went up to the bar to order. The harassed bartender was doing his best to ignore me, however just as I was on the point of giving up and leaving he shot me a "YES?" while mixing several drinks simultaneously, at top speed. I could tell he was ridiculously overstretched, so was prepared to tell him not to worry about it and just go, but he then insisted he'd be able to make us anything we wanted - I'd just have to take the drinks myself to the table. And there was no menu that evening - we'd just have to ask for something we wanted. So I said OK. We asked for Hemingway daiquiris. He didn't know what that was. When I tried to explain, he wasn't really listening. Nonetheless, he persisted in mixing *something* for us, a few minutes later. When I pointed out it was supposed to have grapefruit juice in it, he pulled out a can of grapefruit concentrate, pushed it towards me and advised me to mix it myself! Hilarious, really. I obediently took the can and the glasses back to my amused husband, and we had a nice drink of fruit juice. If there was rum in those drinks, we certainly couldn't taste it! He charged us five dollars in total, which is fair enough I guess - for fruit juice. :) However - we were prepared to give the place another go, seeing as it was Thanksgiving, and he'd been the only bartender for the entire bar and restaurant that night. So we mooched back in a couple of nights later. The drinks we ended up having were mediocre at best, and the bartender that night was equally disinterested and clueless when it comes to artful cocktails. There was some cringingly cheesy live music (thankfully not for too long). The prices are high, the ambiance is stuffy, and the whole place has an overwhelming air of self-importance - entirely undeserved, quite frankly. And the coup de grâce? They state that their (unremarkable) drinks menus have GPS chips embedded in them, so they can track them wherever they be - so WOE BETIDE the hapless thieving customer who just can't *resist* making off with such a treasure! Talk about insulting - and ridiculous! It's a complete lie, of course. What do they do - charge their menus every night?? Now that would be worth the price of a drink to see... There are so many amazing cocktail dens in NOLA. Please don't bother with this one.

text: I'm rarely in the market for art supplies despite being somewhat of an artist (digital guy), I've really slept on this place. For one, I didn't know it was this big. I was on round 2 of trying to get something printed and I had been to most of the print shops in the area. For one reason or another, they couldn't do what I needed done. To my surprise, Blick is the store that would be king. It succeeded where all others failed. I worked in a print shop once upon a time, but that was 10 years ago. I take for granted that things have changed and that surely certain technologies are available just by imagination. To hear the other printers tell it, I was wrong. To hear Blick tell it, I dare to dream again. I knew it was out there and I just had to find it. I needed an illustrator file (.AI) printed in RGB on QUALITY paper in the very same day and for most stores it was near closing time. It cost me a bit, but I wanted what I wanted and needed it when I needed it. Ya dig? The staff was great... not the least bit indifferent or stand-offish. They're genuinely passionate about art. The store was surprisingly sterile. What more could I have asked for short of a La-z-boy and a complementary pumpkin chai? In about 30-40 minutes I had what I needed and I was on my way. I started not to even come in here. I was a few steps from giving up and going home because I had walked right by earlier. Ok... now if I was reading this review monologue style in front of an audience, I'd take a long pause right before this part. Check it out. I didn't even come in here for a print out! text: Looking at the menu I had a hard time deciding on what I wanted, it all looked so good...so I ended up getting the combination platter which consisted of a cup of pulled pork, some slices of tri-tip, four ribs, cornbread, HALF a smoked chicken, and fries (or slaw, beans, salad, etc.) *easily enough for two people (but now I have dinner too!) I'm a pulled pork fan, and this place nailed it; juicy, sweet and spicy. The tri-tip was a little under seasoned, BUT cooked just right, and with the horseradish was excellent! The ribs; oh so much flavor. Not hot (I would have liked a bit more spice), but nice flavor, you really notice the herby notes and rosemary in the rub. The chicken (which I barely dented) was sooo juicy with a mild smoky flavor. And the corn bread is fresh made with chunks of corn in it (not a bagged powder mix), with a healthy pat of honey-butter on top. The fries had a good taste but were slightly on the greasy side. My dad ordered just a cheese burger, said he hadn't had one that good since he was 18 (he's 72)! The service was top notch. Our waitress was very accommodating, and even offered some different beer samples to taste to find out what I wanted with my meat, and she recommended a great one. The atmosphere is about what you'd think for a place called "Men Wielding Fire". Not a large place, maybe a dozen tables. The place is brightly lit up by the huge windows, albeit most the walls are painted black. Chrome diamond plated steel for crown molding. The tables are made of lacquered OSB plywood, cheap to make, but seemed to fit quite well. Overall, a great experience, and I will be back to try out everything else :)

text: Excellent experience, but as a diner, Sbraga breaks one cardinal rule. Last night, my wife and I went to Sbraga, which is Top Chef's Kevin Sbraga's new restaurant that opened last October. Service is attentive, and on par with a four star establishment, so you won't feel forgotten. But lets cut right to it, shall we? The food is excellent, and in nearly all dishes, they were inventive, flavorful, and even whimsical (try the scallop with pressed watermelon, hinted with jalapeño and mint). I had a wedge salad (which seemed like a step down for a spot like this), a sliver of sea bass with pine nuts, and quail with pork belly. Now, all these dishes had excellent flavors (though its hard to screw up a wedge salad). But I left hungry. I get it, its fine dining, dishes are typically small, but even at most fine dining restaurants, your third or fourth course has something a little more substantial on the plate than what was delivered. My wife had one, beautifully cooked scallop, but just one. My branzino, though delicious, looked like it was put through a pasta press. The quail had excellent flavors, but struggled to satisfy, and I found myself picking at the bones, trying to get one more morsel. So my wife and I left Sbraga with a smile, and grumbling tummies. Maybe next time, I'll have a snack beforehand.

text: If only there was an option for 0/5.... Before entering this "jewelry store" I could have never fathomed how intricate and time consuming the request for an appraisal and selling price of my ex's 3 stone diamond ring would be. Having purchased the ring from the same store just a few years back, I decided that I'd return there in order to stay loyal to the local businesses in my area, however I can clearly see why most of the world is purchasing EVERYTHING on the internet. When I entered the store there were 4 employees working and 2 customers ahead of me. It was not until an hour and a half later (that's right, 1.5 hours) that I was given the insulting offer to purchase the ring back from me at approximately 20% of what I originally paid for it. The employees were extremely pushy even before looking at the ring, INSISITING on knowing what I paid for the ring, how silly of me to actually be honest and tell them the real price instead of playing their game. While I was there I witnessed 5 individuals come in the store, and leave after 15 minutes because they were not being offered help by any of the employees. This place is absurd and will use any excuse to get the number they are after, instead of thinking long-term and maintaining POSITIVE customer relationships. The person that finally delivered the amount they'd be willing to buy it off of me for used every excuse in the book, first it was "I have to wait for my boss to get in before offering you a price", after I already heard him appraise the other 2 individual's jewelry. Then it was, "the economy is bad", next it was "we have 20 rings just like this in the back". When I brought up the fact that the price of gold has DOUBLED since I purchased it and diamonds have increased in value significantly since then as well, his excuse was "well there's not that much gold in here". Are you kidding me? I was dumbfounded by that answer. How can a jeweler not understand the fact that no matter how much gold is in any given piece of jewelry, if the price goes up compared to when it is purchased, that INCREASES the value of the jewelry. In hindsight I should have asked him what weights more, a pound of feathers or a pound of gold, I guarantee he would have gotten the wrong answer. I was only planning on recouping 60-75% of what I paid; I wasn't looking to make money off of this ring, I just don't want it laying around anymore because it's just a bad memory. But offering me 20% after waiting an hour and a half is just ridiculous. I guess even local, small businesses are more focused on money and greed than they are on the meaning of the jewelry to the individual and building those solid customer relationships. I do have to say it's a great place to buy Hummel's though, they have an ENTIRE CASE full of them, they haven't sold one in 5 years he said, that is a prime example of incredible business sense right there. text: I finally became a card-carrying NPL member...took me long enough. Only having visited the Green Hills Branch for a meeting, I found this branch to be quite lovely. Inside, there are several kiosks for checking materials in, alongside two desks that allow for human interaction too. The building is spacious, with an airy feel to the architecture (which feels like a mini version of the downtown Seattle Public Library). Plenty of seating lines the perimeter of the library, including meeting space and private study rooms. WiFi is readily available (full bars!), in addition to many computers available for public internet use. A fan of NPR's "Putumayo's World Music Hour", I was pleased to find a fairly large collection of the "Putumayo Presents" CD's, which I promptly checked out for my listening enjoyment. Be sure to take advantage of the online services, which includes a catalog of all items available at each branch. If you find an item you'd like to check out in another branch, just submit a request. NPL will coordinate bringing that item to your branch for you, so you don't have to drive across town to check it out. Now that's service!

Turns out that sign doesn't mark the location, it is just an informational sign. So I started driving around looking for the real site. Here are my directions: Head south from 610 on Elysian Fields, make a slight right to avoid going onto the overpass. Make a U turn under the overpass. You'll see the center right there. Don't be like me and keep driving back and forth across the overpass, as you'd be tempted to dump your recycling in the nearest dumpster and drive home. The actual drop off center is nothing more than a large fenced area with a few labeled dumpsters, a massive pile of tires, and an attendant. I do wish the veggies would have been served in the dish though, rather than on a separate side plate. They were also a little undercooked, but I'd rather have crunchy veggies than soggy ones. My friend ordered the Cherry Venison special and that was also very delicious. I've only had venison a few times in my life and it was never very memorable, but this dish featured perfectly cooked, thin slices of venison, along with warm tart cherries in a slightly sweet, flavorful brown sauce. The atmosphere is quaint and humble, with a touch of fine dining mixed in. We had decent service, though nothing exceptional. text: Terrain is pretty much my favorite place on earth. I live in Baltimore, so it's a good 1.5 hour drive, but I try to go at least once a season. Terrain at Styer's and the Cafe at Styer's are owned and brought to you by the creators of Urban Outfitters and Anthropologie. So if the lust you feel while gazing upon the gorgeous displays feels slightly familiar to you, that is why. Every season is special at Terrain. Winter brings bulbs for forcing and gorgeous Christmas trees and ornaments for sale. When Spring arrives, flowering branches appear in the displays and the nursery becomes fully stocked. Summer is a great time to choose from the enormous selection of carefully curated hanging plants and succulents for terrariums. Fall is my favorite season at Terrain. They have more pumpkin and gourd varieties than I've ever seen and the crisp Autumn air is intoxicating. You can always find special gifts for yourself or someone else in the store. Kitchen sundries, bath products, foodstuffs, cards, stunning antique furniture, and a build your own terrarium section that will make even those with the brownest of thumbs wish to try their hand at building a terrarium. The cafe menu changes based on the season and offers locally sourced and organic ingredients. You always receive the fresh baked bread though, which is baked and served in a small flower pot. Cold drinks are served in mason jars. The tea selection is huge. The dining room is in an old greenhouse and it is magical to eat under all the tropical blooming plants. Reservations for the cafe may be made on OpenTable. Terrain, both the nursery and cafe, is an experience I'd recommend to pretty much everyone. I dare you not to fall in love with this place.

They even have a popcorn butter flavored olive oil (say what?? I can eat butter and improve my heart health??). Then come the crazy balsamic vinegars. What a list we have there! White and dark vinegars from various parts of the world, made in a traditional Italian style. The mission fig balsamic vinegar is my favorite dark one while, the alphoos mango balsamic is my favorite white vinegar. If you are like me and like to spend money on food - you will love this place. If you're not in a position to spend that much but are still curious, come and give the oils and vinegars a try. The helpful staff will blow you off your feet.

text: Freddy's is another new burger-chain entrant to the Tucson market with yet another take on hamburgers. I finally got a chance to check out Freddy's after several earlier failed attempts where I simply bailed out due to a line around the building and the chaos inside. This part of Broadway is ground central in the fast food wars, and the sheer concentration of contenders all within a block of each other will likely soon give way to a shooting war between Culvers, In-N-Out, Five Guys, and Freddy's. At first glance, Freddy's seems a lot like a strange facsimile of Culver's. They both emphasize frozen Custard and both serve burgers, superficially you'd think that the resulting product would be much the same. In reality, Freddy's ends up feeling like a weird cross of Five Guys and Culvers, rather than something uniquely different. First, their burgers are extremely thin. Like super, super thin. I ordered a double California style and was shocked at how thin the meat was, it's like a double somehow becomes the equivalent of one patty at this place, but it's still ~$8 for the combo. In addition, just like at Culvers, there's there's a crunchy substance at the edge of the patty which I'm not a fan of. The consistency of that crispy edge always been a huge turnoff for me, although I know this is a style of burger (the smash technique) that people seem to be a fan of, apparently from the midwest/east coast. I'd expect the smash technique to be the style at a place like smashburger (given the name) not at a place named steakburgers (given the name, I mean, c'mon). The same applies to the fries, which are very thin and crispy. I'm personally not a huge fan of this variety of french fry, but at the same time it's something different. I could forgive extremely thin fries were they all extremely long or around the same shape, instead they all seemed to be different lengths, including some that were very short. Overall eating the fries was just a tedious exercise that I wanted to be done with rather than an accessory to the main event. The name Steakburgers is pretty much an oxymoron -- the burgers aren't steaks at all, being paper thin, and I really have to question why a place named Steakburgers doesn't have steak fries (you can get regular fries, or regular fries with cheese, or add chili, but not steak fries?). None of this makes any sense to me, but maybe I'm just confused and have meat sweats. Maybe it's the weird five guys crossed with a 1960s diner faux-retro decor dulling my senses? Maybe it's because my stomach is still somewhat empty? Maybe I'm having an existential dilemma this is just a greater symptom of, who knows anymore?! No, seriously, I wanted to like Freddy's, but this is the first of the new entrants into the Tucson market that I'm honestly not a fan of. Eating here made me crave Culvers, and after exiting I literally just drove to Culvers with a friend. It's like a better version of the same thing and at least they bring the food to you.

text: The town of Phoenixville, PA definitely is like a phoenix rising from the ashes. The towns' main street (Bridge St.) is wonderful. Daddy Mims is nicely decorated, clean, and friendly. Cajun/Creole food is inspired by the French cuisine. We both ordered the Tour of New Orleans and unsweetened iced tea. When a restaurant charges $100+ for dinner (2 people) you should expect perfection. Daddy Mims got the French Bistro part of SUPER SMALL portion sizes to a tee. First Course: Creole Seafood Gumbo - The soup was flavorful but barely coated the bottom of the large soup bowl (maybe 4 oz.). The crab meat was all broken up from stirring the pot. Where is the andouille and okra? Second Course: Commander Palace style shrimp remoulade - There were two large shrimp (yes two !!!) on the plate with a nicely spiced remoulade sauce and garnish. Taste was good what there was of it. Shrimp cocktail usually comes with six shrimp. Do you think they could at least serve four shrimp? Third Course: Shrimp etouffee served over jambalaya and Cajun style roast pork shoulder with smoked bacon over mashed sweet potatoes - Once again, two large shrimp on about 1 cup of jambalaya. The jambalaya was flavorful but unremarkable. I make better jambalaya as does Zatarains. Next to the jambalaya was about 1 cup of mashed sweet potatoes with a small amount (maybe 1 oz.) of pulled pork shoulder strings. The sweet potatoes were excellent. Fourth Course: White Chocolate Bread Pudding with whiskey sauce - This desert is to die for. I can not say enough about how GOOD this was. Go to Daddy Mims just for this desert. Skip the rest of the Taste of New Orleans. Yum !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Beverage: Unsweetened Iced Tea - The tea was weak. The tea bag was waved across the water. Sweetening options limited to sugar and Equal. Luzerne Tea is available in this part of the country. Luzerne is a southern robust tea not like a woossie Tetley. The service was very good to excellent. On a Sunday evening there were four two-top tables (besides us) and a party of six table being served. Maybe the crowds are getting the feed bag on somewhere else before coming to get the bread pudding desert later. Rating (max 4 stars): Overall - 2 stars. Value - 0.5 star. Food - 1.5 stars. Service - 3 stars. Atmosphere - 2.5 stars. Finally, I will never pay $40.00 for the Tour of New Orleans again due mainly to the portion sizes. If it were not for the desert this meal would have been a total rip-off. Americans want a good meal, large belly busting portions and low low prices. We are NOT the French !!!!!!!!!!!!

text: I can't believe there's only one review for this place as of today. Every time I go, it's packed. Doesn't matter what day of the week it is. This is a very interesting place. Eclectic, edgy art on the walls. Brightly colored. The patio is lovely. Several fans/misters all around so even the hottest days are bearable. They have great margaritas. Several different flavors of the frozen variety, but their house on the rocks is the way to go if you're looking to be impressed. Tons of different beers, both bottled and on tap. Very friendly bar tenders. The salsa. Guys, I'm a big fan of salsa. I've never had warm salsa before, and if I had known that's how it was served in advance I may have been a little apprehensive about trying it. But it is amazing. Fresh and full of flavor, I usually fill up on this stuff and chips LONG before my food arrives. That being said, I have very little to offer in the way of entree review. I've eaten a full meal here twice. The food was good, but I can't remember what I had either time. That either means it was just ok and not impressive or that I had too many margaritas/beers and the entree portion of the evening is foggy. Knowing my weakness for the salsa, I tend to come here to hang out with friends and have some drinks and some chips and crack...er...salsa. I found out recently that they have free wifi. This is just an excuse for me to go there more, because I can legitimately schedule meetings there or convince friends to go because they can still work on projects or whatever. It's pretty loud, but that's cause it's always crowded as I mentioned earlier. Both times I've eaten a full meal here it was with a sizable party and they accommodated us both times. You have to wait, but with the aforementioned salsa to appease you this is a non issue IMO. I've had trouble parking every time I've been here, but honestly it's not their fault. They've got a decent amount of spots in their own lot, plus there are the spots on the neutral ground. I guess there's just so many things to do and places to go on Harrison that it makes parking a bit of a challenge. Don't let that deter you, though. Check this place out. Salsa!

text: Tavern (used to be Lime, which has moved) is great! It is an M Street restaurant, along with Whiskey Kitchen, Virago and (their "crown jewel") Kanye Prime steakhouse. First of all, I love the location. It's right on Broadway - near Patterson, 12th South, Red Door, etc. Second, it's trendy enough without feeling overly pretentious. I dig the layout - there are two outdoor seating area options (which we didn't do because of the cicadas), and the inside is very well done. There are TV's all over the place, the bar is stocked, and there is a decent amount of tables. Third, the service (for us) was very good. Granted, we went on the Sunday before Memorial Day - so it was relatively empty, but still. Our server was attentive, but not overly so where you feel like you couldn't enjoy your meal in peace. And forth, the cuisine. I would describe their menu as all over the place goodness. :) It's so varied, but it all sounds great. APPS: We've heard many good things about the guacamole, so we tried it: The Bazooka Guacamole - with avocado, goat cheese and pistachio. I liked the creaminess of the guac, but wanted more spice / flavor. Luckily for me there were three different hot sauces available labeled as X, XX, and XXX. Yum. (PS - there is also homemade BBQ sauce.) A lot of other app options sounded great, too. We'll probably try something else next time like the Lobster Hushpuppies or the Eggrolls. ENTREES: I was so overwhelmed with the variety on their menu, that last minute I went for the Tavern Burger with White Cheddar - and I switched the Belgian Fries for the Tennessee Fries (sweet potato with jalapeno ketchup.) . The fries were great, and the burger was one of the best burgers in N'ville. My husband was deciding between three completely difference options as well: The Basket of Fish, the Nachos with Pork or one of the Taco options. Like me, he ordered last minute and got the Pork Nachos. I doubt he would have if he had thought about it for even a second since we already ordered the guac which came with a bag of chips...but c'est la vie. They were delish. LIBATIONS: Some of their drinks were pricey, some were reasonable. Just be cautious when you order because your bill could add up quickly if you get the specialty cocktails... I got a $7 glass of wine, and my husband got a beer for $4.75. Comparing Tavern to similar places, it seemed okay to me. :) LATE NIGHT: From 11PM to 1AM they have a late night menu. WEDNESDAYS: 2-4-1's. I'll be returning to Tavern for sure.

text: Ninja is my go-to for "regular" sushi. If I'm feeling fancy, Horinoya. If I'm feeling douchey (just kidding - but the pulsing dance music is so lame) Rock'n'Sake. My boyfriend and I go here probably once a month. The quality is consistent and the service is great. The chefs are friendly and helpful and always willing to make adjustments for you. We always sit at the bar and I've noticed that service is a bit more detached when you choose a table. Edmund is the chef we normally pick, but the owner Momo is pretty masterful as well and we'll always have a soft spot for Moriaki (he left a few years back, but the special roll that's named after him? AMAZING) We rotate through a number of favorite rolls and dishes, so here's the skinny on our faves: *Tuna Box - pressed crab & rice topped with buttery tuna, roe & green onion *Special Crunchy Roll - crab roll topped with fried tempura and 4 sauces *Spicy Salmon Roll (add cream cheese) - spicy fresh salmon with cream cheese and avocado *Moriaki Roll - tuna, salmon & yellowtail with clover sprouts *Goma Miso Roll - crab mix served with a unique miso dipping sauce *Rock'n'Roll - tempura shrimp served with a tangy roe sauce *Cajun Tuna Tataki - seared tuna with cajun spices served with ponzu sauce and green onion *Okra & Asparagus Tempura - deep fried split okra and asparagus spears *Baked Yellowtail Neck - crispy, meaty and flavorful baked yellowtail *Ninja Salad - cucumber and crab-based salad with roe and creamy wasabi dressing My boyfriend also raves about their udon, but I can't seem to order anything else when I go there because the sushi is so delicious. I've heard a lot of mixed stuff about Ninja, but as someone who has been a regular for over 5 years now, I have to say it's the best value for quality sushi in New Orleans.

text: Let me start off with the good - the staff were extremely welcoming and friendly and the salon was clean. Unfortunately - that is where the good stuff ends.
