The two stations are set in the back of the salon in a very tiny room. The manicurist took me back right away and after more than a few trips to gather supplie, started the ped. The ped would not have been so bad but for the fact that the manicurist took a phone call and sent four text messages (using the old flip phone without a key pad no less) in the middle of my service. It was very distracting and unprofessional. Then there was the staff talking about a bladder infection right outside the room while my manicurist yelled from her spot to join in the conversation. Then she proceeded to tell me all about her daughter's problems with yeast infections and ear infections during her youth in excruciating detail. Ugh. After the ped was over - the manicurist said she would take me to her station and then come back to clean up. So I stood up and waited. She then proceeded to clean and sanitize the station (which was nice to see) while I stood there. Having never been to the salon before - I had no idea where to go. At one point, she looked up and apologized for leaving me standing there. But she then proceeded to finish cleaning before simply pointing me towards the front and telling me what chair to sit in. I was standing there so long - I was asked twice if I was waiting for a shampoo. As the manicure began - I noticed she was giving me a regular manicure. I said that I was supposed to get a full set - according to my coupon. The owner - who was doing a manicure next to me - said that Shellac is only for natural nails. But then why would the coupon say "full set?" She said that means it is for all ten fingers. Really? Is anyone coming in for less than all ten fingers? To me - full set means a full set of nails but the owner responded that "anyone who knows Shellac" knows it is only for natural nails. Guess she told me huh. So okay - I will get a regular manicure with the gel polish. Not what I wanted because my nails are very short but I was told "oh. short nails are in right now." Fine. The manicurist then brings over this little plastic bin with about 5 colors of the gel polish to choose from. And the bottles were covered in dust so I am guessing it is not a big seller. She also brought over the box containing one nail dryer. I am already asleep by this time. She then proceeded to do one hand at a time and literally watch the clock tick down while it dried under the light before doing the other hand. The manicure took just over an hour! It was painful. And the worst part is - the manicure was terrible. The gel was on my skin and did not cover the whole nail. I know I should have said something when I was asked how everything was but truly - I just wanted to get the heck out of there. And it last a whole 2 days before starting to peel off. text: I have a beef with Reserve. I came here for a couple reasons. The first was their advertised Mad Men party. The second was so I could show my girlfriend that going to a steakhouse is a worthwhile dinner outing. To address the first: as soon as we got there at 8 (the supposed time of the viewing party), I asked about the free appetizer and specials we were supposed to be entitled to for this event. We were told A) the viewing wouldn't happen until 10, because that's when AMC plays Mad Men (fair enough) but also B) that there would be no free appetizer (a "misprint" that they meant to have taken down, they said) and that we'd only be entitled to the advertised specials while sitting at the bar. We didn't feel like moving so that was out the window, too. Now, Reserve is pricey. I knew that going in. What I didn't know is they serve Voss water. Voss is a premium bottled water (at 7 dollars for a liter or so, not priced on the menu) which is supposedly artesian, but in fact comes from the municipal tap in Norway. If I had known the price and quality, I would have just bought more drinks. Let's talk about drinks. I ordered their Memphis Mojito, because I had never had a mojito with bourbon in it. There was no bourbon in this mojito, in fact, I sincerely doubt there was any alcohol at all. It looked crystal clear, with no hint of the darkness that bourbon would provide. It also tasted like sugar water with mint and probably was. Thankfully, they had a half-decent draft selection, but for a place that prizes themselves on two things--bourbon and steak--their cocktails were a disappointment. The steaks range from the mid-30s to somewhere to the fifties, depending on what cut you choose and in which of 5 styles you want your steak served. I ordered the New York Strip "American" style, which comes with beer battered onion rings (which were bland) and an admittedly gigantic baked potato (Served without butter or sour cream, though? Come on). The steak was served in a veal au jus which I found very tasty, and fortunately for me, it was cooked as medium rare as I ordered it. My girlfriend wasn't so lucky. There was a long black hair in her food. This is completely unacceptable for such a supposedly classy establishment. Naturally, I notified the manager when she walked by, and my grilfriend's steak was replaced. The replacement steak, however, was way overcooked. She asked for medium rare, like me, but received a steak which was well done on one side and medium or medium well on the other. The manager had the decency not to charge us for the steak, but in reality, this should have never happened in a place like this. At the end of the evening, Mad Men finally came on. After rolling the projector screen down for a couple minutes, they retracted it. I guess they figured we were the only ones who would care. But, just like the executives at Sterling, Cooper, Draper, Price, my girlfriend and I have no tolerance for this failure to deliver, especially on such a slow evening. Next time I'm thinking about going out for steak, I'll think again.
label: NEG

text: This is the perfect example of what I imagine a middle-aged mainline business man or some other local variety of briefcase monkey thinks of as "hip". Very nice looking interior screams of overwrought dollar signs: sleek looking but soulless and obviously the product of restauranteurs with FAR too much money to throw around. But none the less, nice, new, clean, innocuous-looking place. A few TV's playing local sports teams behind the relatively small and forgettable bar. Never have I seen so many service personnel standing around-nice to have a server to customer ratio of 1 to 2 I guess, but again, inefficiency and money-hemorrhaging abound. Beer selection is sub-par, mostly macro and a few typical craft offerings. I suppose cocktails are the reason people go here? And I can't objectively comment on this as I did not partake. Food was a crippling disappointment- not just for the selection (which was as trite and antiquated as can be, by the way-the negative tone has nothing to do with volume of selection, as I also believe elephantine novel-sized menus are about as appealing as anal-exploratory surgery ) or the menu design, or the plateware, but the quality was utterly insulting and pathetic. I ordered the Vegetable Platter (I believe that's what it was called) for I think $10. What arrived was a row of hackneyed selections, 3 of which I can GUARANTEE came straight out of a #10 can from either Sysco or US Foods: roasted red peppers julienned straight from the can (I could taste the tin flavor still-not even doctored up with a basic marinade), pickled cauliflower, and some kind of (likely) Tuscan-style white bean preparation. The other components were broccoli rape which had absolutely no seasoning, and grilled scallions/baby leeks, which again had no discernible seasoning or adornment. All this was served with what I can only gasp in horror to say was a single slice of diner-style toasted white bread. The whole thing tasted of refrigerator-burnt margarine or incredibly cheap butter which is stored unwrapped in a refrigerator. Absolutely insulting to someone who has been a professional chef for over a decade; unforgivably bland and boring. Prices were definitely high for the above described food. Beer was priced on par with local places, cocktails/booze I can't say. Laughter is the only response I can justifiably give when asked about this place.

text: Dined here on a Friday evening over the Labor Day holiday. We made reservations via Opentable which was key, as the place was packed and we never saw a vacant table. The main dining area is attached to a relatively open kitchen. The dining area has extremely high ceilings and is dimly lit. The tables are somewhat close together, however you don't feel like you are sitting on top of each other. It's a good date spot. The boyfriend and I each decided to do the $39 per person tasting menu. Before getting to the food, I must mention the drink each of us got and enjoyed immensely. The "Smoke on the Water" was absolutely fabulous. Complementing the liquor was a devilish combination of pepper and lime. This drink is smooth (and potentially dangerous). Luckily, I was able to keep it to two during dinner. Before the mezes arrived, the salatim and hummus arrived at the table with a seasoned laffa. The beets, the carrots, and the eggplant were standouts for me. The hummus was probably the best I've ever had. The mezes were all wonderful. The fried cauliflower was so unique as these golden nuggets sat in the bowl, you wondered what type of fried taste it would have. It's a surprisingly light dish. Another standout was the watermelon and feta salad. I also loved the chicken liver mousse on challah bread which had been lightly grilled. For the main course, I had the duck kebabs. I've never seen it on a menu and was excited to try it. It did not disappoint. The ground duck was perfectly grilled as kebabs and came with rice. After the main course, we were both nearing max capacity, but definitely wanted to sample some dessert. We each got a dessert. The stone fruit came with a nectarine sorbet was a great palate cleanser. We also got the chocolate almond cigars with chocolate mousse. It was hard to go wrong with either of those. Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience. Two small knocks on the place. 1. It was absolutely freezing at our table - bring a sweater just in case. 2. The background music was a tad too loud.

text: The best quality Urban Grub has to offer is the building itself. I absolutely love the architecture and decor. Between the four of us, we had the trout, chicken flatbread, peel and eat shrimp with "gazpacho" (a tiny little ketchup sized dish that was NOT gazpacho), and the prime rib. The trout was good, nothing earth shattering to write about. The prime rib was tough and came out pretty rare (actually I love it rare), but I didn't order it and it was supposed to be medium. Prime rib should melt in your mouth, but this one required as much chewing as a T-bone. I had the Pimm's cocktail, and it's entirely possible that I just don't like Pimm's liqueur, so I won't hold it against them that I found the drink pretty nasty. Not to mention, it took 20 minutes to get iced tea and my cocktail. Overall, the experience was disappointing. I feel like this place has a lot of potential, so I hope they will improve. But as of now, I did not feel like the food met the expectations or cost.

The dip was excellent and to our waiter's credit, he did bring us over extra crostini after we ran out. Usually small plates run between $5-8, maybe up to $10. But Robust had several on the menu for $14...for a tasting plate! We were dumb enough to order one of them - the pork - so I was expecting some pretty amazing pork. It was so dry and so not worth it. Way, way, way overpriced. The flatbread was good, but again at $14 for a small flatbread, way too expensive. At this point I've already invested a lot for a very mediocre dinner so I figured might as well go for broke and order dessert, maybe that can be their saving grace. We both got the fruit cobbler. Again, this whole time our waiter has been AWOL and neither of us have good feelings about him. When we both order the same dessert, he chooses that moment to try to start bantering with us and calling us boring for both getting the same thing, telling us we need to try the bread pudding. Well, maybe if the bread pudding wasn't paired with nasty dreamsicle I would have. And don't suddenly try to be all jokey with us after ignoring us for the past two hours. Unfortunately, but not surprisingly, the cobbler was a disappointment. It was basically baked sliced apples with vanilla ice cream. No cobbler was to be found. Three hours and $80 later we managed to get out of there. I hate to give such a nasty review for a place I've only been to once and judging from the other reviews our visit was not the norm. But with that kind of first impression I will never go back. For $80 we could have had an amazing meal elsewhere. Such a disappointment. :(

In fact, Gino, the owner, is almost always there and he makes a point of coming around and talking with everyone sometime during your meal. He is genuinely interested in how you like your food and wants to ensure that you enjoy your dinner. The food is great -- not fancy, not "over-produced," just good simple southern Italian cooking (like Mama made -- no pun intended)! We especially love the shrimp mumola (appetizer) -- I would serve it on pasta, if I could! Also, the chicken parm, the lasagna, the baked ziti, the veal & peppers, the meatballs... well, just about everything, really. And the house salad with the house balsamic dressing is the perfect counterpoint. In addition, they bake their own bread and serve it up with an olive oil, fresh basil and fresh garlic dip that is habit-forming. We like Mamma's so much that we decided to have our wedding reception there at the end of next month. Nothing fancy... just good friends and good food, and lots of love. Just like Mamma Rosa's. :o)

The place is small, but they have a big enough table for lunch with a few friends. Location-wise it's close to Downtown and South Tampa - easily accessible from a bridge in the middle of the two. Parking is in the street - you might not be able to park in front, but there are plenty of public parking spots in the area. Overall, this place has plenty of different Asian dishes at affordable prices and with great tastes so I will be back for many more trips to this Asian spot on Davis Island. Make sure you sign up for a rewards card! Fun fact: Soobak means watermelon in Korean.

text: I needed to get out of town and St Louis is a great place to go with kids. We decided to book the Hampton because of it's central location. We got a suite since we were going to be there for 3 nights and I would be sharing a room with my SO and 2 kids 4 and 6. The suite is spacious! Very clean, trendy furniture- Including a fridge and sink in the front entry - which is kind of a bar area that I used as a makeshift kitchen/pantry. The beds were comfy but smaller and harder than we were used to. The kids did fine but my SO ended up sleeping the last night on the couch, which he found more comfortable. The staff was super nice and very helpful. The first morning they were slammed during the breakfast rush and so they were out of a lot of stuff, but the other two mornings were fine. They have the waffle maker in addtion to hot suff which changes. One day was scrambled eggs, potatoes and bacon. Another was cheese omelets ( not good - bad cheese) sausage and waffle sticks ( over done). But what do you expect? If you don't have time for breakfast, they have a brown bag packed with fruit, water and a cereal bar you can take to go on a shelf at the front desk. The pool was excellent, clean, not too much chlorine and there were a bunch of noodles and kick boards for the kids- which I thought was a nice touch. The hot tub was big. We swam a lot. Free cookies available at the front desk in the evenings. They had old photos of Forest park when it was an amusement park all over the hotel which was a nice change from the usual hotel crap art. I used the internet a few times and didn't seem to have any problems with speed. We never had a problem with parking. Only drawback was that they missed cleaning up the room after the first night but that wasn't a big deal to me and they cleaned up the rest of the time we were there. I will stay here again and would definitely recommend it.

text: My favorite restaurant in the Quarter! Mona Lisa holds a ton of nostalgia for me. I've been known to eat here twice in one week. Even cheeseless, it's delish, loaded with toppings of your choice and the sauce is downright *zesty*. Fast forward a couple years and *close your ears my vegan friends* the cheese makes it even better. I also had a garden salad so I'd feel less guilty about scarfing down all those carbs. It's a huge green glory and comes with dressing on the side. Besides the food, I've always loved the cozy, romantic atmosphere. It's tiny, intimate and you might see Lady and the Tramp sitting at the table next to you, if you're lucky. Oh and you're surrounded by molto Mona Lisas on the walls, her eyes always following you, the way ML's eyes are wont to do. She's looking down on all of us as we scarf down slice after slice. But there's only acceptance and merriment in those eyes...

text: I really want to like this place but I just don't get why people love it so much. First of all it is expensive to get it, which is not a deal breaker by any means but I do expect that for a $10 entry fee I am going to enjoy myself. The 10 story slide is a bit of a trek to get to but in the end you think that it is worth it. For me, it was not. Maybe because I am a little bit taller, about 6'2", I am too big for this thing but I did not enjoy going down it at all. I lifted my knee for a second and smacked it on the roof of the slide and really wasn't having a good time going down the slide. Other than that and the caves there really isn't much to see inside. There are a few things here and there but really unimpressive to me. The outside can be fun, which is the only reason that this place even gets 2 stars in my mind, but that doesn't make up for the lack of anything else to do there. Also, the 4th floor being a used clothing store is just strange and I am not sure why that is there. Why would I pay $10 to go to the city museum and then have the urge to buy used clothes? Everyone seems to love this place, so maybe this is just me, but really save your money and go almost anywhere else in this city. So many great things here are free, basically anything if Forrest Park, and there are much better places to pay to go to. Also, take my review with a grain of salt as I am 23, most kids would probably like the place a lot more than I did so it is probably a great place if you are younger.

text: Food is very good (used to be fresher).....Salsas are excellent and therein lies the problem. They just started serving chips a couple of years ago charging $2.00 for a modest amount....this in itself is very rare in Mexican restaurants and recently jacked that up to $2.50.....WOW!!! Back to the salsa issue....it's a serve your self salsa bar with one size container that holds about 1 tablespoon and is just wide enough to dip a french fry in. Not conducive for a happy chips and salsa experience. Very frustrating for a serious salsa aficionado. Management must have had a few or more complaints on this because they came up with the idea to issue a larger, user friendly disposable paper bowl and charge an additional $1.00 for it!!! Folks, this is a taqueria not the Taj Mahal. If you eat often at taquerias you expect to get in and out for less than $10.00. Now if you are at El Bajio and order chips you have spent $3.50 already so you have $6.50 remaining.....that won't even buy you a burrito here. I am not certain why the management chooses to annoy and gouge its customers over something as simple and pleasing as chips and salsa but the word greed comes to mind. What else could it be? You don't have to be a food service expert to recognize that a modest amount of chips and salsa costs about 50 cents to produce at the very most including food, labor, and overhead. Selling it at $3.50..... You would expect to see finger prints from Wall Streeters all over this. If you elect to eat at El Bajio and forego the chips because of my incessant whining I hope you thoroughly enjoy your $8.50 burrito. Again, their food and salsas are VERY good. Oh, and by the way there are about 7 other Mexican restaurants on Milpas Ave. in case you decide not to support the greedy one. Amen Amigos

text: Anyone worth their high blood pressure knows Philly's best sandwich is the roast pork. I'll never fully grasp why the cheesesteak would be printed on our $1 bills if we became our own sovereign nation because the flavors of pork are far more interesting and tasty. Differences in cook temperatures, marinades, and seasoning create more room for a better sandwich. Compare honor roll student sharp provolone against the short bus services of whiz and all doubt, in my minority opinion, is removed. This proliferation of great roast pork makes it easy to spot impostors; the bad ones that have the authenticity of fat Vegas Elvis impersonators. This is George's. The pork tastes like it was marinated in water. The broccoli rabe fails to add its trademark bitterness and if the sharp provolone was a knife it would struggle to cut its way through warm butter. If you're thinking about George's, you're thinking about the Italian Market. That's the good news; your thoughts have plenty of room to wander elsewhere. Let them take you away from this place.

text: A while back I gave Kentwood a solid four stars. Today I would give them zero if that were an option. Kentwood Ford and Ford of Canada absolutely refused to fix the power steering under warranty. Their reason: My last service was not at Kentwood but rather at a quick lube. Power steering pump failure at 63,000 km is premature. Work order says they replaced the power steering pump, rack, lines, and did a four wheel alignment. At a total cost of over $2,300. I launched a complaint with CAMVAMP, a federal government organization that oversees vehicle manufacturers and their warranties. Today was my last visit ever to Kentwood Ford. text: Another 'meh'. Damn. I hate writing mediocre reviews... I started with a veggie roll, and had a 'Spicy Cashew' meal, generally served with chicken- but subbed for tofu. The roll was delicious, very fresh and not too big. Usually a veggie roll is overstuffed to the point of difficult to eat, but this one was perfect- avocado, asparagus and carrot, rolled lightly in sesame seeds and drizzled with some type of unmemorable sauce. The cashew plate was good, with mushrooms, baby corn and broccoli- all sauteed wel and tossed in a not-so-spicy sauce with some cashews.... It was a little saddening. 'Spicy' on a Thai menu is usually more exciting than that... Not here. Oh well. The service was good, and the iced Thai coffee was great... The bill was the deal breaker. $8 for my veggie roll. I can usually get out.the.door. at Little Tokyo (not including the bottle of wine that I take in...) for $8. I'm a vegetarian for christ sake- theres nothing fancy in there! I've never paid more than $4 for a veggie roll- and they're usually 2x the size (and hence difficult to eat). Ouch. The plate? $14, plus an additional charge for tofu. Hm. Sub tofu instead of chicken. Not tofu AND chicken. Hm. Fair's fair- it was printed on the the menu- but really? The portion nor quality were not NEARLY worth $16- let alone the cash I saved them on chicken. All in all, I felt as though I'd been bled dry for a measly meal. The place is cute, clean, and friendly... But c'mon guys- there is too much competition for this to be acceptable.

text: Hoss' Loaded Burgers can be followed on Twitter for current locations @hossburgers (or http://www.facebook.com/hossburgers). Anyhow, I had Hoss' Loaded Burgers recently when they were parked outside the Jackalope Brewery one night this past week. I tend to follow most of the food trucks in Nashville on Twitter, so I saw that the Hoss would be nearby. I initially thought to myself that I didn't want a stuffed burger for dinner. What would I be doing to my calorie count that late at night? I thought to myself, but you just worked out like an hour ago... you. cannot. do. this. to. your. arteries. But, then common sense prevailed and I realized that someone calling themselves a "Hoss" couldn't possibly lie to me. I HAD to try the place. Plus, I love food trucks. I had a burger stuffed with jalapeños and gouda topped with bacon and lettuce and smothered in some sauce that was delish. I also got a side of the parmesan cheese and rosemary fries, and a side of the sweet potato fries - because I was feeling indecisive as evident from my earlier internal conversation with myself about even having a burger that night. Burger cooked medium - check. Burger served atop toasted bun - check. Burger inside goodness oozing out with the first bite (because remember the burger is stuffed with something... in my case gouda and jalapeños) - check. Served to me in a reasonable amount of time, given they did have to cook a burger through medium. Overall: recommend and enjoyable.

text: Hello - Food and Jazz fans. Although we are not avid reviewers of the many businesses ( restaurants) that we frequent, last night's dining experience at this bistro deserves mention. Before the 10 PM jazz performance, we wanted to go to Adolpho's across the street but since they had a 40 minute wait, we decided to try the bistro part of Snug- after many years. It was Thursday nite, 8PM, 50% tabled patrons. Firstly, there was one female and one male server who both did well handling their load. Our female server was adorable, efficient, polite. The two of us ordered a Caesar salad with house dressing; fried calamari, Rib Eye steak with sauteed mushrooms and a 'loaded' baked potato, paired with house Chard and Abita amber. Here's what we wound up with. 1). We brought our own wine and was told that there would be a $20. corking fee !!! I said, what if it's a 'screw-top'. She said either way, [ you'll get 'screwed' ] since that's the price of THEIR cheapest bottle. 2). The Caesar salad was NOT suitable for Caesar himself and would have resulted in the cook's beheading for serving mainly romaine lettuce stalks with a mound of (pre-bagged) croutons. The dressing was decent and obviously bottled. 3). The $11. Calamari was an insult. It was a (generous) portion of bagged pre-cut, pre-breaded, fryer flash dropped small pieces. Upon complaint, the misinformed server said, "that's the way it's done in New Orleans". She was politely corrected. 4). The $30. Rib-Eye steak was menu touted to be [a delicious cut, well marbled, better piece of beef]. Ordered med. rare, a decent sized portion arrived properly cooked, but lacking any meaningful seasoning, marinade or garnish.( $30.!) The 'marbling' was 30% fat and grizzle. The tenderness was fair. 5). The sauteed mushrooms were admitted to being from the can. 6). The 'loaded' baked potato was of the sister estab. Port of Call fair-good standard. Summary: It ain't what it used to be. They seem to have structured their kitchen, offerings and procedures to a tourist crowd turnover who are hurried, and not looking for (or aware of) a good only (not great) dining experience. I can understand their protocol, but the prices are NOT commensurate with quality. What was disturbing to my wife is that the popularity of Frenchman street should offer our food conscious tourism guests a better sampling of a quality or fair value meal. How hard can it be to prepare a fresh, in-house salad dressing, with fresh toasted croutons on a bed of trimmed romaine ? Or, saute a fresh, sliced shitake mushroom ? A popular dish like Cal, (presumably like their fish) could be fresh, sliced, gently breaded and fried. Our sweet server recognized our comments and admitted to the shortcomings, would no longer offer the Cal. and removed the Cal and shrooms from the bill. She still got a 25% tip on the balance for good service, personality and spirit. If it's jazz and drink your after, this is a cool spot. But if you want good food at a fair price, move on, up or down the block.

Its an innocuous looking bean soup, then you taste it, and get a mouthful of savory porky bacony essence that make you feel a little guilty eating such rich dish. I am not giving this place a perfect 5/5 since there are comparable places in the neighborhood that are less famous, and therefore, less wait time. This location is fantastic. Everytime I go in here I get greeted with friendly faces and enthusiastic attitudes. Everyone here seems to really enjoy being here. I find that refreshing. Once here I needed some Tobasco (Green). The manager just gave me a whole, unopened bottle. It was amazing. I know, it's a little gesture, but it made my day. Another time here, I had gotten my order, made it through the line and realized I had forgotten my wallet at home!! Right, now what?? The kid told me to just take it and have a great day. I was thrilled by the generosity. Luckily, I found a twenty I had stashed in my car, so it worked out for everyone. Go to this location. I moved into the city, so now Clayton and U-City are my frequents, but I still go to this one everytime I'm on that side of town.
label: POS

text: I called Friday evening to get a reservation and to inquire that if our 8 yr old granddaughter didn't find anything on the menu could we give her some food that we brought along. I really wanted to try 943 and was hoping they would. The young person on the phone said emphatically that we could. When we arrived our server immediately focused in on our granddaughter (I'm sure she was the one I spoke to the night before) and asked about her likes regarding spaghetti. She knew that if she took care of her first that our evening would go smoothly. We were very hungry and the salami and cheese and the bread and pepper/oil were so wonderful. We ordered empanadas for our first and would have loved the grilled octopus but it wouldn't be ready until we were long gone since it had not arrived at the restaurant in time for earlier preparation. Bummer. My husband loved the asparagus and skirt steak and my daughter and I ordered the ravioli. Sat. night it was filled with crab and lobster and had a light tomato cream sauce. I could have licked the plate. I had heard the chocolate molten cake was fabulous (and it was), but I had to try the Italian lemon cookie. It was filled with yummy caramel and dusted with powdered sugar and fresh coconut. I wish I had taken some home. Our server opened our bottle of wine and our order taking and service was perfectly paced. We never had to ask for service. She came back to the table frequently but not obnoxiously so. When we were seated at 5:30 and when we left at 7 there was only two tables of two vacant. There was also two tables of 10-15 (friends celebrating) and the noise was nominal. They didn't bother us at all. I would think our slurping might have bothered them. I have heard that they slow to start and I hope that they continue to get better and more business so that when we come back to Philly (we live an hour away) to sight see with the grand kids that we can dine there again. Really...a lot of places have a cash only policy and I mean a lot. I can't understand why anyone would be pissed about that when they should have checked it out before hand. We always do. This place is so worth patronizing and I can only imagine that something was off the nights that other diners experienced. It shouldn't be-no excuse for Pascal-but our experience was stellar. Keep trying.

text: We had a good stay overall despite small problems through out the stay and I would return. We stayed here for two nights, our first night we arrived early morning, we decided to park in the Mansion house. First of all the garage is a bit confusing if you've never been and hard to find an exit to walk out of ( we learned to park near the entrance if possible so we could walk out through there than go through the side stairs that smelled of urine or "pissy stairs" as we called them)but alas you get what you pay for so I didnt' expect much more than to save $. When we got checked in the lady checking me in wasn't very personable but wasnt rude or anything, maybe it was due to us being there at 5 am, not many people are awake at that time. As we got in the elevator to go upstairs the power went out and of course I wanted to get out since the elevators doors had closed and I thought we were stuck, but all I did was push the help button and the elevator doors opened and I was extremely relieved. Of course once the elevators were back up I was a little scared to ride it up to our floor but I did fine. The common areas of the hotel were nicely done, very classy and the room was nicely decorated, up to date, and we had a partial arch view. Same day but much later.....our room wasn't cleaned when we arrived after being out the whole day so we were a little disappointed in that but all it needed was to have the beds made so it wasnt a big deal. Our second night I will have to say I saw an influx of people, seemed like a lot of college or baseball fans, one or the other. That night we were woken up by someone pounding on a door and shouting to be let in, I thought someone was surely trying to break in. It was our lovely neighbors who were having some kind of lovers quarrel, three guys trying to get back in their hotel room and a mad girlfriend not letting them in or something along those lines. My bf went out and set them straight and they left. Well I finally dozed off and again we hear this damn pounding loud enough to wake us up, I guess guy is finally allowed in but I still call front desk. Third time woken up is when security knocks on their door and they come out and speak so freaking loud I wake up again. Fourth time I hear a large group of girls and guys shouting. laughing, and interacting with the idiot next door. If it wouldnt have lasted less then a couple minutes security would have been called again. The rest of the night was fine but dealing with this definately put a damper on my night. The next day when we checked out we explained the situation and security had the info to back it all up. We were given a credit to one of their restaurants so I appreciated their effort since they didnt have any control over their rowdy guests. Overall the hotel was in a nice location, great rooms, not such great neighbors if you get the college crowd, but overall since I got a deal on priceline I'd say it was a good place to stay and would return.

text: Loved it. This was one of the best brunches I've had in awhile, if not ever. This isn't your traditional eggs benedict spot or a place to get $6 eggs with meat and potato. It is, instead, an experience from beginning to end. The atmosphere is casual and inviting yet sophisticated. The service was top notch, not stuffy, and very attentive to water and coffee glasses the entire time. A key to quality service is the top-off of coffee after you've signed the check; our water and coffee remained fully attended-to until we left. I had the Fresh Baked Biscuits & Gravy with pan fried lamb sausage, tomato "gravy", and spicy hot pepper jam. Phenomenal. I could eat this every weekend. The biscuits were a touch dryer than I would have normally preferred on their own, but they worked perfectly well with the gravy and jam. This is one of those dishes that you will crave and I hope it doesn't disappear off the menu. The garden brunch with seared scallops and a farro salad, with veggies, and lemon and chive vinaigrette was also a favorite at the table. Four scallops seared perfectly for a tasty and satisfying, yet light, option. We had to try dessert right? The meyer lemon ice cream with toasted angel food was out of this world, perfectly tart. The chocolate pudding tart was also amazing, served warm with pumpkin ice cream a dash of salt and caramel. A perfect ending to a perfect brunch. Our tab with coffee, entree, and dessert (including tip) came to about $40/person. A must try for brunch and I can't wait to sample their dinner (and their great outdoor dining space in spring/summer!)

There was a cool engineer's room that you could peer into on your way into the hotel from the parking lot. It's in walking distance to almost any place you could want to go in the French Quarter. Negatives: The room was small, and the bathroom was even smaller. It was a little tight for three people. Maybe we got one of the lower-end rooms, but my friends weren't too impressed with it -- which is what you want to like since you're probably spending more time there than the lobby! There was a working mail chute outside the room. It was $34 plus tax for guests to park in the hotel. Maybe that's normal for NOLA, but that seems kind of high!

text: What a way to cap off an OUTSTANDING week in New Orleans by taking a friend's advice and trying the Praline Connection! Located a short walk from Jackson Square and right on famed Frenchman St, this place was easy to get to and allows you to feel less guilty about "indulging" as you walk back through the French Quarter to your hotel. I got to try the Chicken Livers (which I love anyway). This is a HUGE portion for an appetizer, not that I'm complaining! I hated to eat all of 'em myself.....but I DID! Crispy, tasty, with a bowl of pepper jelly/sauce for dipping gives it a great flavor and a nice "bite." Breaks my heart (not really) that my wife doesn't like livers..... We both had the po'boys; mine was oyster, hers was shrimp. Both were served on fresh baguette bread, dressed. The oysters were big, crispy, and delicious! I'm almost thankful they didn't come with fries so, be forewarned, you have to order that extra. She then ordered bread pudding for dessert (my dessert was the remaining livers). However, I did get to try a couple spoons of it. WOW! LOVE the praline topping they put on there and the rum sauce was excellent! Perfect finish! Prices were very reasonable considering their location and the service is top-notch. We'll definitely be back.

text: I love coming to the Reading Market. Yes, it's hustle and bustle and a fight sometimes for the food you want. Come early to avoid the crowds...before noon on the weekends. If you want the breakfast at Amish Eating Place, come when it opens. Don't expect gourmet food here, but expect good, hearty local fare and great fresh produce that is discounted when the market is about to close. Some notes: Bassetts--it's not the creamiest artisanal ice cream around, but hey, it's part of the Philly experience. I had the pomengranate berry chocolate chunk and it satisfied my ice cream craving for the day. Amish bakery counter-for some reason, the men seem to ignore me when I go to pay. The women are much more customer service oriented. I have tasted many of the pastries--they are cheap and taste it. Too much sugar and too little butter. I usually only get the breads with glazed toppings. The other goods are nondescript. And what's with all the unhappy children forced to work so early? Child labor??? During Amish week in PA(in July), don't miss the fried doughnuts. They are divine. Le Bus-this place got some bad reviews from other Yelpers. I've never had a bad bread or bagel here. I love the cherry apple bagels and the olive bread. The day I waas there, they had a low turnout and too much inventory so they were discounting their bread at the end of the day. Whoohooo.... Flying Monkey-the cupcakes are good but just okay for the price. Metropolitan Bakery-prices are higher; everything they sell is delectable. Termini Bros.-how can you sell sweets and be so snotty and rude? Someone should send all the servers to customer service class. Are their pastries good? Sure? But I've walked away from this place at least 3 times when I was ignored. And if you're selling biscotti at $20 a lb, you need to smile. The chocolatiers Muellers etc....-if you are in to high end gourmet chocolate, take a pass. If you just want a piece of Philly traditional chocolate, go for it. Eating area--needs more cleaning people! Bathrooms-try to find someone else to go. I do! Oh, and if the crowds dismay you, Chinatown is just around the corner.

text: You've never had an authentic fish taco until you've been to Oscar's. I have tried fish taco's everywhere searching for the best... and I finally found it. Here at Oscar's. I don't know why I waited so long to try this place. Well, I didn't live in Franklin until this year, but still, I've been in Nashville for eight years and only recently heard about this place. This place puts SATCO to shame and is better than any fish taco you get at a "nicer" sit down tex mex restaurant... probably because this place is actually owned operated by a mexican! This hole in the wall is a hidden gym. I tried a fried fish taco and a chicken taco (made with fajita chicken). Both were succulent and amazing, but the fish tacos are to die for. I love the "special sauce" they put on the fish tacos. The fish taco was so good, I may not ever try anything else on the menu... I'll be getting two fish tacos from now on. But I wanted to try something else on my first trip. Oh, and two tacos is plenty of food... they fill 'em up! Pros: A la carte menu of burritos, tacos, and more. Excellent price/value. Food of course is amazing. Cons: This location only has fried fish (I like fried just fine, but a grilled option would be a plus).

Anyway, I decided to wait for my appointment in the quiet room. This room is called the quiet room for a specific reason, one would think. But as soon as I settled into a chair, I heard bursts of laughter and greetings from behind the wall. From what I observed, the employees room is behind the quiet room, and there is a hallway leading to it that runs along the wall of the quiet room. So, as I'm sitting there, I'm hearing employees come and go, laughing and greeting each other in a very loud way. Do they not get that the quiet room is just on the other side of the wall? Anyway, I had a nice facial, and decided to sit in the jacuzzi for a bit, and that was nice. They also provide cucumbers for your eyes, along with iced wet towels to lay over your eyes. I lounged in a chair with the cloth over my eyes and relaxed for a bit. When I got dressed to leave, as I passed the inner reception desk, there were several employees hanging out there, chatting and laughing quite loudly. You could her them all the way back in the changing room. I've been trying to decide if this visit was any better than the last one. I just don't understand the management not teaching the employees to keep their voices down. I have even spoken to friends, trying to decide if I'm being unreasonable, and everyone I talk to about this agrees with me. Spa environments are supposed to be quiet. Period. I thought Jessie, the manager I spoke with when I booked the appointment, might follow up with me, so I waited to write this review. text: I really do like the asiago bagels here but I absolutely abhore the service. The counter is staffed mainly by teeny boppers who give off an air of affected ennui and can't even take orders correctly over the phone. I called in the morning to preorder a dozen of the asiago (this was at 8 am, mind you) and was put on hold for 15 min while the girl chatted with her counterparts (I could hear them in the background) about non-bagelry related issues. She then proceeded to get back to me with a "I'm not sure."" Um, honey, you should really find out what your employer's policies are since you DO work there. I assured her that I have preordered bagels here numerous times. She then proceeded to take my order. Okay, phase I over. I told her that I would pick them up at 1 pm. I showed up at 1:30 (to give them some extra lead time) to find the register unattended and a group of teenages gathered in a huddle chatting. I literally stood there for 10 min before one of them noticed and asked if I needed anything. I should note that it took her 10 min to locate my order and another 10 to ring it up. I did get my bagels in the end but next time, I'll just volunteer another poor soul to pick them up and deal with the atrocious service. The bagels are pricier than South St. or NY Bagels ($1 each, $12 for a baker's dozen), but it is the only non-chain place in the area to carry asiago bagels (I know that they aren't real bagels but we still love them all the same) that aren't simply steamed pieces of dough topped with a few shreds of cheese. The texture is excellent: perfectly soft on the inside with a chewy, flavorful exterior shell. The sandwiches are good, but they are pretty expensive compared to the other cafes in the area; the prices are almost as steep as Spread's but the Kosher breakfast bagel is very good ($6 for Nova, cream cheese, sauteed onions, and egg on an everything bagel) and hard to resist. It's also one of the relatively well-priced options; most lunch sandwiches are $9. There is so much potential but they do need to work on their customer service quality and maybe adjust the prices so that they are slightly more reasonable (I understand that it's about quality and taste but paying $10+ for a coffee and breakfast sandwich is kinda outrageous).

text: You go down Ranstead street haldway to find a small row house with no signs. You know you're at the right place because there's a slightly industrial door for what should be the front door. You go into a dark foyer light by a glowing red bulb before pushing through the peak windowed door into the main bar. I can best describe it as entering the bat house at the Zoo...you go into a quiet and dimly red lit room that is the barrier between the real world, and a stranger place that feels slightly like a dream. Inside, the walls are lined with velver wallpaper and adorned with pin-up style paintings. There are plush booth to slip into, or pull up a stool at the bar so you can survey the whole room. The music can only be described as eclectic. You feel like you're in a 1970's movie, but it's not cheesy or gimicky. The barternder's moustache and suspenders are real, the extensive use of vinyl and velvet somehow work, and you feel like you're in another time. There are plenty of interesting concoctions you've never thought of, so order 1 or 2 to start off with, but by the time you're ready for third, live on the edge a little and order the Bartender special. He'll grill you with a few questions before making you something that would have probably sounded unappetizing in print, but it delicious once it hits your lips. I was given a Manhattan made with Tequila and chocolate...amazing! If you go, be sure to be patient as it's a very small room and hard to get a seat. You can leave your cell # with the bartender and they'll call you when there's an opening. An excellent place to take a date for good conversation, odds are she's never been here, let alone even heard of it, and regardless of what else may be going on, you don't even think about there possibly being something better going on anywhere else. Once you go you're torn between telling all your friends what an awesome place you found, and never telling them so you don't spoil it's charm.

text: Look, it's expensive. But they specialize in high-end cars and you get what you pay for, so let's get that minor quibble out of the way and dismiss it early, because you'll pay the same or more at a dealer anyhow. Now that we've covered that... Is it weird to love your mechanic? I mean, not in a chocolate and flowers way or anything, but that immense satisfaction in the knowledge that you're in good hands, the work will be done correctly, and the shop knows the vehicle. I discovered Dearing through a recommendation by Dave Radmacher. Dave is tied up with the local Porsche Club chapter and works on all the older air-cooled models. The newer water-cooled owners, he sends the way of Dearing, and vice-versa. So we begin with PCA-SAR approval, and that's kind of a big deal. I was in there for a clutch replacement, and they mentioned the intermediate shaft bearing. It's a costly replacement, and I think they're blowing smoke up my rear because we're all conditioned to think the mechanic is screwing you, right? Well at this point a gentleman behind the counter begins to hand sketch a perfectly intelligible diagram that explains everything, what model years were affected, when Porsche corrected it and how, etc. This guy KNEW what he was talking about! (And after using some Google-fu, I verified the potential problem.)These guys don't lie to make a sale. They suggested it because where they were working on my car was right next to the IMS, and I'd save money on the labor vs. doing it later. I opted not to, due to budget, but I remembered. Then when I picked my car up they were washing it and finishing buffing/drying the wheels. I took my car back for an oil change later. They washed it again! They do it every time as a courtesy. How could I not begin to love this place? Coming up on a major service interval, I inquire about doing the IMS bearing now. They tell me the cost of the part is cost of the part, and this service interval doesn't get into that area of the car, so labor would still be expensive... And then they offer to cut me a deal on the service interval itself, to help ease the blow. They're a business, here to make money and provide livelihoods to their employees, and they do exemplary and deserve every penny they earn- but still try to cut their customers a break. Quality of work and attention to detail? These guys are absolutely worth what they charge. And if you're a car guy, going here is sometimes like a museum visit, getting to sneak peeks at Ferraris and even a Lamborghini Countach. Dearing Automotive is one of the things I miss most about Tucson, and I've considered making the drive back from Las Vegas, NV just to have them work on my car. They're that good.

Everything is a la carte, so bring a well-padded wallet or credit card account. Dinner rolls were tasty with a crusty exterior with soft interior, served with virgin olive oil and pepper. We also asked for balsamic vinegar, which is so good with olive oil. Gary's French onion soup was the winner, hands down! A generous crock with baked-on cheese arrived. My mom's bean and ham soup was also tasty, with a light clear base. Just watch out for some fatty ham pieces (used to season it, I'm sure). I ordered a basic salad with a delicious (citrus?) dressing. It was a great mix of greens and veggies, including arugula. We had been tempted by some entrees we saw listed on the Entertainment Book page for Azul, but found that the menu had changed and those dishes were no longer offered. The meals we purchased ranged from $19 to $28. Gary's chicken was tasty and mom's sea bass was served filet-style at her request (normally served tail-on & head-on). We opted not to order the side vegetables, which sounded great, but we did not think we'd have room for them ($7 each side). The service was friendly and prompt. We enjoyed our meals and that great view. It is a bit upscale in cost for a la carte and the portions. See photos. I would suggest the restaurant consider adding some greens or rice-or something-to the plate to give it some substance. text: When I was very young and living in Sacramento, my mother joined a meditation group following an Indian guru (this *was* California in the 80s). She went to meetings at the house of a beautiful Indian woman named Nanda, whose house always smelled wonderful and who would make chai for the children to drink while the parents practiced meditating. The first time I visited Sher-E-Punjab, I found myself thinking about those times quite a bit while we were waiting. It seemed sort of odd, as they occurred when I was only six or seven and my 'memories' might be more accurately described as 'vague impressions', but once the food arrived I chalked it up to the vagaries of my brain and dug in. The food was amazing, and well worth the slightly-long wait - a wonderful mixture of spices and textures that was hot, filling, delicious, and somehow reassuring. Even the spiced rice was wonderful, and I'm not usually a fan of the stuff (much to the dismay of my half-Japanese husband). When we finished, I asked if they served coffee to go with dessert. They didn't, but said they had chai instead, and I gladly took them up on the offer. When they brought it out, suddenly the memories came flooding back, and I realized why I'd been thinking so much of my early childhood - it was exactly the same style of chai that Nanda had made for me, all those years ago. Very likely the owners were from the same region of India, and the smells had been reminding me of her house without my even realizing it. I've been back several times since then, and I'm pleased to report that the food's held up even past the childhood associations. My favorite by far is the lamb masala, made with some mysterious blend of saffron and cardamom and cilantro and tomato and cream that somehow makes me nearly orgasmic with happiness. Sadly, between the slow service and the nickel-and-diming price structure (I love the garlic naan but man does it add up fast), I don't feel quite justified giving them a full five stars, but the food makes them well worth going to despite their flaws.

We are serious sushi eaters and have tried all others in the area. The rolls were just amazing, large, fresh, and very fairly priced! The Triple Threat appetizer is a must try. We ordered 10 different rolls. The 8 piece rolls had 9-10 pieces. All delicious, larger pieces than any other sushi place around, and very very fresh! The spicy scallop hand rolls...off the charts!! If you are a sushi lover like we are you owe it to your taste buds to try Jimmie's. Oh and don't judge a book by it's cover! We knew it was there for over a year and never thought to eat there because of the plain, ordinary looking signage out front. It just didn't look like a place we would want to try. Boy were we ever surprised! The inside is decorated beautifully, clean and very comfortable. They have 4 gorgeous salt water fish tanks with some amazing tropical fish, Big screen TV's and really comfortable seating. Now let's talk service. The staff is above and beyond friendly from the moment you walk in the door. Jimmie is such a nice guy, and makes you feel like family right away. you can taste the care and passion he puts into his Sushi. we used to eat at Osaka Sushi in Madeira Beach often. No need to go back there again after trying Jimmies which has much better Sushi, more generous portions, and better prices. Winner winner sushi dinner....Jimmies is amazing!

text: Heirloom surprised me. I only realized it existed a couple days before actually going. Turns out it's a polished BYOB right next to Wine & Spirits. Dining room is obviously a complete overhaul and has a sophisticated outdoors feel. Menu casts an eclectic net of inspiration. Some twists they had on southern cooking looked very good. Short rib ravioli was a little different than I had envisioned, with one large pouch filled with short rib chunks among other things. Cherry sauce and onion jam was very good. I wanted the venison and chestnut crepe. Actually, I really wanted it. Unfortunately, others also really wanted it and it was stricken from availability. So I was forced to get the roast lamb. Life is hard. It was only delicious. Red honey chili glaze worked very well. Eggplant and tomato stack was flavorful, and sauteed grapes are always hits.
